articles.title: ¿Y si Vinicius vuelve a bailar?
articles.standfirst: William Hill te ofrece las mejores cuotas del mercado
articles.summary: William Hill te ofrece las mejores cuotas del mercado
articles.body: Cuando todo parecía perdido, Vinícius ha recordado por qué fue segundo en el Balón de Oro de 2024. El brasileño cerró el parón internacional con cinco goles en dos partidos con Brasil: un doblete a Japón y un hat-trick en doce minutos ante Singapur, el primero de su carrera con la selección absoluta. Lo hizo justo antes de regresar con el Real Madrid tras cumplir una sanción de cuatro partidos, y con un arranque de temporada de un gol y tres asistencias en 12 encuentros que ha disparado las alertas en las casas de apuestas para el Balón de oro. William Hill sitúa como favorito a Lamine Yamal, a cuota 4. El extremo del Barcelona fue segundo en 2025 y tercero en 2026, y mantiene un nivel de regularidad que ningún rival iguala a su edad. Esta semana dio además el pase del 2-3 de Nico Williams ante Inglaterra, aunque el Barça llega con dos derrotas recientes, el Clásico y la Champions ante el PSG. Su precio es el de un candidato que parte con ventaja, pero con un margen de beneficio muy ajustado. Kylian Mbappé es el segundo, a cuota 5.5. El delantero del Real Madrid suma once goles en Liga y acaba de ganar el Clásico, además de formar parte de un equipo con una racha de victorias consecutivas. Fue segundo en la gala de 2026, y su cuota refleja que el mercado lo ve como el rival más serio de Yamal, aunque aún le falta el título colectivo que suele inclinar la balanza. Michael Olise aparece a cuota 9. El extremo del Bayern cerró 2026 en el noveno puesto y vive una evolución constante en un equipo que pelea por todo. Su precio premia a un jugador en ascenso, aunque tendrá que superar a varios nombres con más pedigrí. Jude Bellingham comparte esa cuota de 9. El inglés no entró entre los diez primeros de 2026, pero su potencial como centrocampista decisivo, con un gol y cinco asistencias en cinco partidos con Inglaterra, mantiene viva su candidatura. Es la apuesta de quien cree que el Madrid le dará la plataforma que necesita. Raphinha se paga a 10. El brasileño del Barcelona llegó a acumular 17 goles en 12 partidos esta temporada, una cifra extraordinaria que sostiene su candidatura. Su cuota refleja la duda de si podrá mantener ese ritmo durante todo el curso, y de si el voto se repartirá con su compañero Yamal. Vinícius cotiza a 21, el precio más alto de la lista, y ahí está la gran pregunta del mercado. Su cuota, dentro de las apuestas deportivas, se explica por el mal inicio con el Madrid, agravado por la sanción de cuatro partidos tras su expulsión ante el Villarreal, que le dejó sin jugar contra Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing y Valencia en Liga, aunque sí pudo disputar la Champions. Su regreso será el 21 de noviembre ante el Celta en el Bernabéu, un partido que servirá para comprobar si sus cinco goles con Brasil se traducen en un cambio de rumbo con el equipo blanco. Los antecedentes no ayudan: Vinícius ha recibido críticas por no repetir con su selección el nivel que muestra en el Madrid, y ahora le ocurre lo contrario. De cara a las apuestas, conviene recordar que el Balón de Oro se decide en la temporada completa, y que un buen parón no garantiza una temporada de campeón. A cuota 21, Vinícius es una apuesta de valor para quien confíe en que el brasileño recuperará el nivel que le llevó a pelear por el premio hace dos años, pero con un riesgo evidente: necesitaría dispararse en Liga y Champions desde ya. Los favoritos, Yamal y Mbappé, ofrecen más seguridad, aunque con menos premio. Con seis meses por delante, las cuotas pueden cambiar de forma drástica.

articles.title: The Top Playmakers And Breakout Stars Who Made Our Nations League Top XI
articles.summary: There were some truly magnificent performances in the UEFA’s Nations League.
articles.body: There were some truly magnificent performances in the UEFA’s Nations League and as we say goodbye to the group stage, I think it’s important to highlight the very best examples – because some of them were perhaps career-changing. There were players who took on the role of vindicator, especially in hostile environments, whilst others continued to remind us of the consistency of their brilliance and how, in the words of Aristotle, "We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit." articles.title: El cantante Blessd es el nuevo dueño del Deportivo Pereira
articles.standfirst: Blessd y su mánager compran el Deportivo Pereira y son los nuevos dueños
articles.summary: Blessd y su mánager compran el Deportivo Pereira y son los nuevos dueños
articles.body: El fútbol profesional colombiano vive un remezón histórico y mediático. Stiven Mesa Londoño, mundialmente conocido como el cantante de música urbana Blessd, y su mánager y socio Santiago Jaramillo Morán, popularmente llamado Dímelo Jara, dieron el gran salto para adentrarse de lleno en la propiedad de un club histórico del rentado nacional: el Deportivo Pereira. Tras semanas de rumores y negociaciones que sobrevolaron los despachos del Eje Cafetero, la operación se concretó en una notaría de la capital risaraldense, donde se firmaron los documentos decisivos que traspasan la mayoría accionaria del cuadro matecaña al grupo empresarial del artista y su representante. La noticia comenzó a tomar fuerza luego de que se confirmara la reunión entre los nuevos inversores y Álvaro López, el hasta entonces máximo accionista de la institución (quien poseía el paquete mayoritario desde octubre de 2022). En el encuentro notarial, respaldado por figuras del gremio ejecutivo como el expresidente de Atlético Nacional Juan Carlos de la Cuesta, se selló la cesión de la gran parte de las acciones que controlaban el destino del conjunto risaraldense. Si bien Álvaro López conservará una participación minoritaria dentro de la nueva estructura societaria, el control administrativo y mayoritario pasa a manos del tándem conformado por Blessd y Dímelo Jara. La llegada formal del nuevo grupo directivo busca inyectar estabilidad y aire fresco a una institución que ha atravesado turbulencias financieras en los últimos años. El Deportivo Pereira recibe a sus nuevos propietarios en medio de desafíos administrativos urgentes. En los meses previos a la compra, el club debió lidiar con complejas situaciones económicas, incluyendo atrasos en las obligaciones salariales del personal administrativo, demandas acumuladas ante la FIFA y restricciones operativas que afectaron el normal transcurrir de la institución. Con la llegada del capital liderado por el intérprete de éxitos urbanos y su equipo de trabajo, el objetivo primordial es poner al día las finanzas, sortear las demandas internacionales y estructurar un proyecto deportivo sólido de cara a los próximos torneos de la Liga BetPlay. La experiencia acumulada por los nuevos dueños en el ecosistema del balompié internacional se perfila como un soporte clave para encaminar esta transición. Para Stiven Mesa y Dímelo Jara, esta no es su primera incursión en la industria del deporte rey. El grupo empresarial ha demostrado un interés genuino y constante por diversificar sus inversiones en el fútbol internacional y aficionado: Vendsyssel FF (Dinamarca): En octubre de 2024, el artista y su mánager adquirieron el club europeo que compite en el balompié danés. UB Coquense (España): En 2025, Blessd se sumó como inversionista y embajador oficial de la entidad española. Fútbol Sala y divisiones menores: Adicionalmente, son dueños de proyectos como El Carmen Bendito FT en el ámbito local y mantienen una estrecha relación con la representación de jóvenes talentos en diferentes instituciones del rentado colombiano. La adquisición del Deportivo Pereira representa el paso definitivo de Blessd por consolidar su pasión por el fútbol —la cual ha manifestado públicamente desde los inicios de su carrera artística— transformándose ahora en el máximo responsable institucional de uno de los equipos más carismáticos y tradicionales del Eje Cafetero.

articles.title: Roll The Tape: Vikings-49ers Is Immovable Object Vs. Unstoppable Force
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 10, Bucky Brooks examines three new developments to watch.
articles.body: The NFL's most explosive offense is taking on the league's stingiest defense. Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay is pulling off new tricks. And a new star wide receiver is emerging in the AFC. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are three developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.What Happens When An Unstoppable Force Meets An Immovable Object? We'll soon have our answer as the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) take on the Minnesota Vikings (7-2) in Week 11's International Game in Mexico City on Sunday night. NFL fans, scouts and coaches alike will appreciate the whiteboard wizardry of San Francisco's Kyle Shanahan and Minnesota's Brian Flores. The 49ers enter Week 10 ranked first in total offense (399.4 yards per game) and second in scoring (31.2), with Shanahan's clever scheming often leaving the defensive coordinators and defenders dazed and confused at the snap. His heavy use of pre-snap motions, heavy personnel groupings (two wide receivers or fewer) and exotic run-play designs with complementary pass concepts makes it hard for opponents to diagnose plays and find the ball. Moreover, the organized chaos created by the Niners’ pre-snap movement and post-snap execution can leave defensive coordinators scrambling for answers on game day. "Where do I start?" Flores told The Athletic. "Everything (on the 49ers offense) is high level. It's thought out. There's a rhyme or reason behind it all. Complementary plays … from a run-game standpoint, it's elite. From protection, it's elite. Play design is elite." It's high praise coming from Flores, who enters the game with the league’s top-ranked unit in scoring defense (14.0 points) and sacks (37.0), while also surrendering the second-fewest yards per game (273.3), with a blitz-heavy approach that has earned the mad scientist rave reviews from football enthusiasts around the globe. The Vikings’ radical game plans feature a mix of five- and six-man zone blitz pressures designed to dismantle pass protections and run-blocking schemes with creative movement from aggressive defenders intent on getting to the ball at a breakneck pace. With offensive coordinators unable to prepare their troops for unpredictable blitzes from unique pre-snap alignments, the Vikings are forcing playcallers to use small menus, letting Flores adjust quickly in-game to the opponent’s approach. As a result, the Vikings often dictate the game’s flow, while putting quarterbacks under immense pressure to make sound decisions under duress. The mental and physical toll of playing Minnesota routinely leads to critical errors at pivotal moments from both experienced and novice quarterbacks. Based on 49ers QB Brock Purdy’s struggles against the Washington Commanders and DC Daronte Jones, a former Vikings assistant who previously served as the team’s defensive backs coach/defensive pass game coordinator, the Vikings’ pressure package could disrupt the MVP candidate’s rhythm within the pocket, leading to a subpar performance from the fifth-year veteran. Against the Commanders in Week 5, Purdy was blitzed on 41.5% of his dropbacks and completed just 6 of 11 passes (54.5%) for 86 yards, per Next Gen Stats. It was the first time Purdy failed to throw a touchdown against the blitz in 2026. To help his QB find his way against the Vikings’ relentless pressure, expect Shanahan to feature more empty formations from heavy personnel (2 wide receivers or fewer) to keep the defense in a base alignment, while putting San Francisco's best players in better position to succeed. With running back Christian McCaffrey, tight end George Kittle and fullback Kyle Juszcyzk making it work with their versatility and interchangeability as playmakers, the heavy package might be the best way to counter the Vikings’ blitz-heavy tactics on the perimeter. Additionally, the 49ers will release five eligible receivers into the route to maximize their chances through the air. Against the Vikings, the decision to release everyone into route will force Flores to decide how he wants to handle empty formations and running back routes from the backfield under maximum pressure. If he continues to apply the pressure with "peel" principles — where an edge rusher or linebacker matches the running back if he releases on a swing or flat — the 49ers can take advantage of the concept with angle routes or options that allow CMC to work inside and away from the defender. Although few teams have opted for this tactic, the 49ers believe in populating their route concepts with five eligibles, and the Vikings’ aggressive scheme won’t discourage Shanahan from staying in attack mode. In the running game, expect the 49ers to steal a page from the Detroit Lions’ playbook and run more "insert" plays with multiple tight ends or wide receivers leading runners through holes in the tackle box. In Week 8, the Lions used the tactic successfully to help Jahmyr Gibbs to a prolific performance on the ground (153 yards and a score) against the Vikings’ radical approach. Given Shanahan’s desire to get CMC untracked to help control the game, the 49ers will use Kittle and Juszczyk as lead blockers to give them a numerical advantage at the point of attack, while creating room for their RB1. In a game that should be viewed as a chess match on grass, Shanahan’s ability to manipulate his pieces through clever alignments and formations might be the deciding factor in this NFC heavyweight battle. 2.Who Needs Elite Receivers? Not HC Sean McVay Credit Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay for adapting his offensive scheme to maximize his talent. With Davante Adams and Puka Nacua sidelined with injuries, the Rams (6-4) leaned into their "20" personnel package (two running backs, no tight ends, and three receivers) to keep the Cardinals on their heels in Week 10 and extend their four-game winning streak. While Arizona had to deal with a heavy dose of "13" personnel (one running back, three tight ends, and one wide receiver on 63.5% of snaps, per NGS), the Rams also deployed "20" on 17 snaps, totaling 197 yards and a touchdown. Given that they hadn’t shown the two-back personnel grouping before Week 10, the element of surprise helped the Rams take advantage of an opponent that wasn’t prepared to deal with a two-back passing formation. In studying the film, the Rams’ use of running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum is sensible because it puts a better group of players on the field. Additionally, the subtle personnel change makes it tougher for the defense to match up in base or sub-packages. The thought of a "BOB" (back on backer) situation in space should terrify defensive coordinators uncertain about how to handle a two-back running game that also features a myriad of backfield motions from the halfbacks. Whether motioning the back out wide to the nearest sideline or crossing behind the quarterback to become WR3/WR4 in a spread alignment, the creativity of the "20" package might be the perfect remedy for the Rams’ receiver woes. Williams and Corum are not only reliable pass-catchers, they're effective route-runners who can set defenders up with head-and-shoulder fakes and hesitation moves to get open in space. Additionally, both backs are effective inside runners from the shotgun, taking advantage of opponents’ wacky pre-snap alignments. With McVay taking more time to explore the package’s potential, the Rams’ split-back package could add another dimension to an offense that is seeking new ways to mask its limitations with both of its star receivers on the sidelines. 3.The Best Wideout You Haven't Heard Of Perhaps I’m a little biased based on my weekly exposure to wideout Parker Washington’s game as the Jacksonville Jaguars’ sideline analyst on radio broadcasts, but the fourth-year pro looks like the league’s next superstar wideout. Washington has been on a heater this season with 36 receptions, 645 receiving yards, six scores and 24 first downs on 64 targets for the Jags (7-2). He is coming off a spectacular performance against the Titans in Week 10 with 152 receiving yards and a score on seven catches. The 5-foot-10, 204-pounder continues an impressive run, having snagged 94 receptions for 1,492 yards and 11 scores since the start of 2025. As the Jaguars’ emerging WR1, Washington has done most of his damage on in-breaking routes, averaging 3.5 yards per route this season, the most among receivers with at least 75 such routes, besting even the Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Washington has totaled 337 yards on in-breaking routes, the eighth-most in the league, accounting for more than half of his receiving yards and four of his six touchdowns. The punt-returner-turned No. 1 option has amassed 155 yards on crossing routes, the third-most in the NFL, with two touchdowns. As a rugged runner with outstanding balance, body control and quickness, Washington runs through arm tackles in the open field, showing a running back-like style that makes him tough to bring down. With a league-high 119 yards after the catch on crossers, the shifty receiver threatens to score from anywhere on the field when he catches the ball on the move. While Washington’s catch-and-run prowess makes it easy for QB Trevor Lawrence to target him on underneath routes, the undersized playmaker has become a dangerous big-play threat as a vertical route-runner. He has torched opponents on post routes, using his speed and leaping ability to win 50-50 balls downfield. Amid carrying the responsibility of a go-to option, he has also shown the ability to win against press coverage. He leads the NFL with a 5.0 yards-per-route average against press coverage, per Next Gen Stats, ahead of Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4). A dive into his film reflects a dynamic pass-catcher with the athletic potential to make his mark as a three-level playmaker. His Week 10 breakout is just a sample of his game-changing potential. With a marquee game against the Giants on Sunday, Washington has an opportunity to earn a greater appreciation for his electric game from the football world. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. articles.title: Cooper Flagg scores 33 as Mavericks keep Warriors winless since Stephen Curry's injury
articles.summary: DALLAS (AP) — Cooper Flagg scored 33 points, P. added 21 and the Dallas Mavericks stopped a three-game losing streak with a 116-94 victory over the Golden St...
articles.body:
DALLAS (AP) — Cooper Flagg scored 33 points, P.J. Washington Jr. added 21 and the Dallas Mavericks stopped a three-game losing streak with a 116-94 victory over the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night.

Will Richard scored 18 points and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 13 for Golden State, which dropped to 0-4 on a five-game trip that started with Stephen Curry tearing an oblique muscle in a loss to the Houston Rockets.

The Warriors have lost by 38, 21 and 22 points in three full games without their superstar, who is expected to miss at least another week.

Kyrie Irving scored 17 for the Mavericks, who led by as many as 29 points after losing by an average of 28.7 points on their three-game skid.

Irving started a 16-2 run early in the second half that featured five different scorers and gave Dallas an 80-53 lead. Washington had a 3-pointer during the run and finished 5 of 7 from deep.

Flagg was 11 of 15 from the field and 8 of 8 on free throws and had nine assists, five rebounds and three steals.

The Warriors shot 24% from long range and scored less than 100 points in a third consecutive game for the first time in almost five years.

It was the first meeting of former Michigan teammates Morez Johnson Jr. and Lendeborg. They were the ninth and 11th overall picks, respectively, in this year's draft after helping the Wolverines win the national championship.

While Lendeborg is clearly becoming a Rookie of the Year contender with the Warriors, Johnson is struggling to have a similar impact. Lendeborg had a rough shooting night, going 6 of 18, but Johnson was just 1 of 5 in 15 minutes.

Warriors: At Memphis on Thursday to finish a back-to-back and the five-game trip.

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen's controversial forfeits spark domino effect! Two more GMs skip games at Total Chess Pilot
articles.summary: World No.
articles.body: World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen's decision to forfeit his Fast Classic games after securing unassailable leads has triggered a domino effect at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot, with two more Grandmasters choosing to skip their matches on Wednesday.India's R Vaishali and Armenia's Haik Martirosyan were left waiting in the playing hall after their respective opponents, Abhimanyu Mishra and Richard Rapport, decided not to turn up for the concluding Fast Classic games. The developments came after Carlsen had courted controversy by walking away from his matches against Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva on consecutive days.While Carlsen's actions had already raised questions about sportsmanship and the tournament's regulations, the decisions by Mishra and Rapport have added another layer to the debate over the format.Mishra explains decision after Vaishali is handed eight pointsCompeting for places 21st to 24th, 17-year-old Mishra entered the final game with an 11-1 lead over Vaishali after winning the opening day's fixture 13-7. He had also secured the second day's match before the Fast Classic encounter, having built an advantage through the blitz and rapid games.Mishra chose not to play the concluding contest, handing Vaishali all eight points on offer. However, his 11-9 victory in the day's overall score meant he won the tie and advanced."There's nothing to say," Vaishali said as she walked away from the playing area.She will now face Uzbekistan's Nodirbek Abdusattorov in a match to avoid finishing last in the tournament.Mishra later took to X to explain his decision, citing fatigue after an exhausting schedule and uncertainty over whether the remaining games in already-decided matches would count towards players' ratings."There's nothing to say" was Vaishali's brief reaction, while Mishra said he had approached the chief arbiter well in advance to seek permission not to play."Well in advance of the next game, I approached the chief arbiter to ask whether it would be acceptable for me not to show up. She told me that the decision was entirely mine and that it was perfectly acceptable not to play," he wrote.He added that the demanding schedule, coupled with uncertainty surrounding the rating implications of the remaining games, had influenced his decision."Given that uncertainty, combined with the fatigue I felt, plus permission from the chief arbiter, I had sufficient reasons not to show up," Mishra said.Rapport also skips game after losing tieRapport's decision came in a different context. The Hungarian Grandmaster had already lost his tie against Martirosyan and was trailing 2-10 on the second day after conceding the opening day's fixture 9-11.He subsequently forfeited the Fast Classic game, leaving Martirosyan without an opponent for the concluding encounter.The two walkovers followed Carlsen's repeated decision to skip the final game against Assaubayeva after taking commanding leads in their two-day tie.Carlsen's actions put tournament format under scrutinyCarlsen had already secured an 11-point advantage on the opening day against Assaubayeva after winning three of the four blitz games and two rapid games. He then forfeited the Fast Classic encounter, handing his opponent all eight points on offer, but still won the day's fixture 11.5-8.5.The Norwegian repeated the move on Wednesday after building a 10-2 lead through the blitz and rapid games. Assaubayeva was again awarded the eight points, leaving the day's score tied 10-10. Carlsen, however, advanced on the strength of his opening-day victory.Explaining his decision, Carlsen said the concluding game had little significance once the match was decided."There will be no classical game as I understood, the match is over. The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally meaningless game," he was quoted as saying by Norwegian broadcaster TV2.Carlsen also admitted that he was not keen on playing more classical chess in the classification fixture."This is an awkward situation to be in, I would rather not play that much more classical anymore," he had said on Tuesday.The Norwegian's decision attracted criticism, with American Grandmaster Hans Niemann alleging preferential treatment and insisting that the rules should be applied equally to all players. FIDE Chief Executive Adviser Emil Sutovsky described the conduct as unsportsmanlike, while India's Olympiad captain Srinath Narayanan also criticised the lack of courtesy.Organisers looking at feedback ahead of 2027 editionThe controversy has also put the spotlight on the tournament's regulations, particularly the significance of Fast Classic games after a player has already secured qualification.Total Chess CEO Kjell Madland said the Budapest pilot was intended to help organisers assess the format and identify possible refinements before the inaugural edition in March 2027."The Budapest pilot is an important learning exercise for Total Chess. While we have developed the format and regulations with considerable thought and input, the real test is how they work in a live competitive environment," Madland said in a statement.He added that organisers wanted feedback directly from players and arbiters before deciding whether changes were necessary.The organisers had not immediately confirmed whether Carlsen's forfeits would attract an automatic fine. With Mishra and Rapport now also having skipped their concluding games, the issue has become more pressing: whether the format needs clearer rules to ensure that every scheduled game is treated consistently, irrespective of whether a match has already been decided.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ¿Qué es el Sandpapergate?: la trampa del papel de lija que no se olvida
articles.standfirst: La biografía de Usman Khawaja reavivara el caso del 'Sandpapergate', uno de los mayores escándalos del críquet en Australia
articles.summary: La biografía de Usman Khawaja reavivara el caso del 'Sandpapergate', uno de los mayores escándalos del críquet en Australia
articles.body: Una hoja de papel de lija, una pelota de críquet y un plan para alterar su superficie durante un partido internacional desataron en 2018 uno de los mayores escándalos de este deporte en Australia, reabierto ahora tras nuevas acusaciones que cuestionan quién conocía el engaño. El caso, conocido como 'Sandpapergate' (el escándalo del papel de lija), estalló durante el tercer partido de la serie de cinco pruebas entre Australia y Sudáfrica, disputado en marzo de 2018 en Ciudad del Cabo, cuando las cámaras captaron al australiano Cameron Bancroft utilizando un trozo de papel de lija para raspar la pelota y modificar su comportamiento en el aire. Para entender la gravedad de lo ocurrido hay que saber que, en el críquet, los lanzadores pueden conseguir que la pelota se desvíe durante su trayectoria mediante un efecto conocido como 'swing', que dificulta al bateador calcular dónde caerá. Cuando la pelota se desgasta de forma desigual, puede producirse además el llamado 'reverse swing', un movimiento en sentido contrario que puede resultar especialmente complicado de anticipar. Las reglas permiten limpiar y mantener la pelota bajo determinadas condiciones, pero prohíben modificar artificialmente su superficie para conseguir una ventaja. Al rasparla con papel de lija, Bancroft buscaba favorecer ese movimiento y ayudar a los lanzadores australianos a eliminar a los bateadores rivales. Las imágenes provocaron una crisis inmediata y una investigación de Cricket Australia, la federación nacional, que concluyó que el entonces capitán, Steve Smith, su segundo, David Warner, y Bancroft habían participado en el plan. Smith y Warner fueron suspendidos durante doce meses y Bancroft durante nueve. La investigación señaló a Warner como impulsor de la iniciativa y a Bancroft como el encargado de ejecutarla sobre el terreno de juego, mientras Smith reconoció que conocía el plan. La controversia parecía cerrada, pero ocho años después ha vuelto a abrirse, después de que el exinternacional Usman Khawaja reavivara el caso en su autobiografía al asegurar que no fueron únicamente esos tres jugadores quienes conocían la operación, sino que todo el equipo estaba al tanto. Bancroft ha respaldado ahora esa versión en un extenso artículo publicado en el diario The West Australian, en el que admite que no contó toda la verdad durante la investigación de 2018 para evitar implicar a otros compañeros y asegura que acabó convertido en el chivo expiatorio del equipo. En su relato, sostiene que las prácticas para alterar el estado de la pelota habían comenzado antes de aquel partido y que, durante el segundo encuentro de la serie contra Sudáfrica, en Port Elizabeth, la presión por conseguir que la pelota se desviara en el aire llevó a David Warner a plantear el uso de papel de lija. El actual capitán australiano, Pat Cummins, que formaba parte del equipo en Ciudad del Cabo, ha rechazado categóricamente las acusaciones y ha negado conocer el plan. También lo han hecho otros integrantes de aquella línea de lanzamiento, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood y Nathan Lyon, que ya negaron cualquier conocimiento del engaño en un comunicado conjunto en 2021. Ante las versiones contradictorias, Cricket Australia ha anunciado la creación de un foro independiente y confidencial para que jugadores y miembros del cuerpo técnico puedan contar su versión de los hechos. No será una nueva investigación disciplinaria ni implicará nuevas sanciones, sino un mecanismo para escuchar a quienes consideran que no fueron consultados en el proceso inicial La federación busca así esclarecer las distintas versiones y cerrar una crisis que va más allá de una infracción deportiva, al poner en cuestión la cultura del equipo, la transparencia de sus responsables y la responsabilidad colectiva en uno de los episodios más controvertidos del deporte australiano.

articles.title: BYD SEAL U DM-i 2027: ¡temblad, SUV híbridos enchufables! El líder se refuerza
articles.standfirst: BYD actualiza la versión híbrida enchufable de su exitoso SEAL U. A simple vista parece que cambia poco, pero tiene más maletero, gana potencia, carga más rápido y su batería es de mayor capacidad
articles.summary: BYD actualiza la versión híbrida enchufable de su exitoso SEAL U. A simple vista parece que cambia poco, pero tiene más maletero, gana potencia, carga más rápido y su batería es de mayor capacidad
articles.body: «Houston, tenemos un problema…». Eso debían de pensar los principales rivales del BYD SEAL U DM-i. Y, después de ver y conducir el modelo de 2027, diríamos que ahora tienen un problema… un poquito más grande. Y no porque el BYD SEAL U DM-i haya crecido con esta actualización. Sigue midiendo 4,78 metros de largo y su diseño apenas cambia. Lo que ha hecho BYD es escuchar las críticas de sus clientes y de la prensa especializada y centrarse en los aspectos que tenían margen de mejora. El resultado es un coche con más maletero, un chasis revisado y más potencia en toda la gama. Vamos, que sus rivales tienen motivos para preocuparse. El SEAL U DM-i fue el híbrido enchufable más vendido en España en 2025 y, entre enero y octubre de 2026, solo lo ha superado su hermano pequeño, el BYD Atto 2 DM-i. Ahora nos encontramos con un modelo todavía más redondo y con un precio que sigue siendo francamente bueno. Sin ayudas ni descuentos, la versión Boost arranca en 39.300 euros. Por fuera cuesta distinguirlo del anterior. La principal novedad es la parrilla delantera activa, que se abre o se cierra en función de las necesidades de refrigeración. También llegan dos colores, el Burgundy Red y el Graphite Blue. Todas las versiones llevan llantas de 19 pulgadas, con un acabado más oscuro en el Design. Por dentro encontramos más diferencias. Toda la gama lleva Google integrado de serie, hay una nueva combinación de tapicería en azul y gris y las versiones Comfort y Design incorporan asientos calefactados en las plazas traseras laterales. Pero quizá lo que más se agradece es el aumento de capacidad del maletero. Ahora ofrece 530 litros en las versiones Boost y Comfort y 510 litros en la Design, lo que supone una ganancia de entre 80 y 105 litros según la versión. ¿De dónde sale ese espacio? Los nuevos paneles laterales permiten aprovechar mejor la anchura y, al rebajar un poco el piso, se gana altura útil. Los materiales son agradables al tacto, su calidad está por encima de la media y los ajustes son buenos. En conjunto, transmite la sensación de estar en un coche bien hecho, con detalles cuidados y un acabado propio de un segmento superior al que uno esperaría por su precio. Es fácil encontrar una buena postura al volante y las plazas traseras siguen siendo bastante generosas. Empecemos por el chasis. La suspensión trasera pasa de tres a cuatro brazos, un cambio que mejora la calidad de rodadura en autopista y ayuda a controlar el balanceo de la carrocería en curva. La dirección, por su parte, incorpora un sistema de doble piñón en la cremallera. Tiene un tacto más natural, permite guiar el coche con mayor precisión y, en zonas bacheadas, se perciben menos vibraciones en el volante. En las versiones Boost y Comfort, el motor de gasolina 1.5 atmosférico de 98 CV deja paso a un 1.5 turbo de cuatro cilindros y 130 CV. También gana potencia el motor eléctrico delantero, que pasa de 197 a 204 CV. Con estos cambios, la potencia conjunta sube de 218 a 238 CV. Ambas versiones conservan la tracción delantera. El Design 4x4 ya contaba con un 1.5 turbo de 130 CV. En su caso, la principal novedad está en el eje trasero, donde el motor eléctrico pasa de 163 a 204 CV. La potencia conjunta alcanza así los 374 CV, 50 más que antes. En cuanto a las baterías, el Boost conserva la de 18,3 kWh y homologa 80 km de autonomía eléctrica. El Comfort mantiene la de 26,6 kWh, con la que ahora alcanza los 130 km. El Design es el que da el mayor salto: sustituye su anterior batería de 18,3 kWh por la de 26,6 kWh del Comfort y pasa de 70 a 114 km de autonomía eléctrica. Las tres versiones admiten ahora hasta 55 kW de potencia de carga en corriente continua, frente a los 18 kW anteriores. Esto permite pasar del 30 al 80% en 15 minutos en el Boost y en 20 minutos en los Comfort y Design. Con todo, el BYD SEAL U DM-i sigue siendo un coche excelente para viajar. Es cómodo, tiene buen tacto y está bien insonorizado, de esos coches en los que los kilómetros pasan casi sin que te des cuenta. Además, con la batería cargada y el depósito lleno, BYD anuncia entre 914 y 1.030 km de autonomía total, según la versión. En ciudad también se conduce con comodidad, aunque sus dimensiones se dejan notar al callejear o al buscar aparcamiento. Quizá sea en las carreteras de curvas donde menos a gusto se siente. Tampoco es el tipo de trazado para el que está pensado y, aun así, cumple sobradamente. En cuanto al precio, la subida depende de la versión: va de los 800 euros del Boost a los 3.000 euros del Design 4x4. A la vista de las mejoras en el chasis, las prestaciones, el equipamiento y la capacidad del maletero, consideramos que el incremento está justificado.

articles.title: De no recibir la llamada de España a brillar con Argentina: el caso Nico Paz, tres años después
articles.standfirst: Pablo Paz ya advirtió en 2023 que su hijo no tuvo que elegir entre las dos selecciones
articles.summary: Pablo Paz ya advirtió en 2023 que su hijo no tuvo que elegir entre las dos selecciones
articles.body: "¿Argentina o España? Nico no tuvo que decidir. La selección española nunca lo ha llamado". La frase de Pablo Paz en Radio MARCA Tenerife en julio de 2023 vuelve a cobrar fuerza tres años después. Su hijo se ha convertido en una de las grandes figuras emergentes de Argentina mientras crece la pregunta sobre qué habría ocurrido si la Federación Española hubiese apostado por él a tiempo. Argentina sí se adelantó. Nico Paz recibió la oportunidad de incorporarse a la dinámica de sus selecciones inferiores y no dudó en aprovecharla. Además, pudo compartir entrenamientos con Leo Messi, el gran ídolo de su infancia. "A Nico le gustaba mucho y pudo entrenar con Messi. Si España lo llamara, no sé qué haría. Si me preguntas a mí, creo que se quedaría con Argentina", explicó entonces su padre. El tiempo terminó confirmando aquella predicción. Nico debutó con la absoluta en octubre de 2024 durante el 6-0 ante Bolivia y dio a Messi la asistencia del último gol. Después dejó clara su elección: "Nací en España y amo a los dos países, pero decidí representar a Argentina. Es el país que más me representa y es un orgullo seguir los pasos de mi padre". Ahora, el tinerfeño ya marca diferencias con la albiceleste. Le bastaron 45 minutos para firmar un doblete en el 7-0 frente a Costa Rica y volver a disparar la ilusión alrededor de su figura. "Representar a esta camiseta es lo máximo", afirmó después de otra exhibición que confirma su crecimiento. Su explosión internacional también ha reabierto el debate sobre el Real Madrid. Nico Paz pudo regresar al conjunto blanco, pero decidió permanecer una temporada más en el Como para seguir siendo protagonista bajo las órdenes de Cesc Fàbregas. Selene Melián desveló en 'La Tribu' que la decisión partió del propio jugador: "Nico Paz ha sido quien ha decidido quedarse este año en el Como. Conozco a Nico y a su familia y sé de lo que hablo". La periodista explicó que el futbolista quiere regresar algún día al Bernabéu, aunque esta temporada prefirió jugarlo todo en Italia antes que asumir un papel secundario en Madrid: "¿A quién quitas para poner a Nico Paz como indiscutible? ¿Quitas a Bellingham?".

articles.title: India clinch historic lawn bowls series in New Zealand
articles.summary: India completed a remarkable turnaround to clinch the three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal
articles.body: India completed a remarkable turnaround to clinch the three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday.Having lost the opening test before levelling the series with a comeback win on Tuesday, the Indian team produced another composed performance to seal the trophy on New Zealand soil.The experienced Jharkhand duo of Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur gave India a winning start, defeating their New Zealand opponents 9-7 in the men’s pairs. New Zealand hit back in the women’s pairs, where Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh went down 2-5.India regained the advantage in the mixed fours as the quartet grabbed a crucial 7-5 victory. The visitors then sealed the overall test by winning the first mixed pairs contest 5-2. Although New Zealand claimed the second mixed pairs match 7-4, India had already secured an unassailable lead and with it the test and the series.The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland. According to Dinesh, belief in their own abilities proved crucial to the turnaround.“We know that if we play our natural game, we can challenge any team in the world. We showed that here. We kept reminding each other to play our best and leave everything on the green. Everyone gave their all, and we achieved our goal,” he said on Wednesday.For Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki, the key to India’s revival lay in the unity shown by the four-member contingent. “The best thing was our unity. None of us made excuses about being tired, lacking sleep or facing difficult conditions. All four of us played as one team. We fought together, came back together and eventually won the series together,” Pinki said.Sunil, meanwhile, underlined the significance of winning the trophy away from home.“The biggest satisfaction comes from winning on New Zealand’s home turf. Winning in India would have been special, but coming here, competing in their conditions and taking the trophy back home makes the achievement even more meaningful,” he said.The series victory provides another significant boost for Indian lawn bowls in what has already been a successful year for the sport and will serve as a confidence booster ahead of upcoming international competitions, including the World Championships.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who wins Fury vs Joshua? The Independent writers predict British super-fight
articles.summary: As Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua prepare to clash at long last, our writers weigh in on the British fight of a generation
articles.body:
On 11 December, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally share a ring, after almost a decade of build-up.

The former world heavyweight champions each make up one half of the biggest British fight of a generation , and opinions in the boxing world are split on the outcome.

Will Joshua's superior knockout power pay off? Or has the 37-year-old become dangerously fragile, an accusation levelled at him after he was dropped twice in round one this July, in a chaotic two-round win over Kristian Prenga?

Will Fury's ring IQ and sharper movement secure him the victory? Or did the 38-year-old's tepid recent wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach show a regression that could equal vulnerability against "AJ"?

Below, The Independent 's sports writers predict December's main event at Cardiff's Principality Stadium.

Alex Pattle, Combat Sports Editor: I think both guys are pretty vulnerable at this stage in their careers, so it might be a matter of who lands cleanest first. I believe the "Gypsy King" is likelier to land the sharper and more frequent shots in the early rounds, so I'll go with Fury to break Joshua down in the middle of the fight . Although AJ hits harder, I also think he's less resilient, so Fury might not need to connect that hard to put him in serious trouble. That said, I can also see a chaotic bout where both men go down, and Joshua has shown he can come off the canvas and still produce a fight-finishing blow.

Jack Rathborn, Sports Editor: I can see why most are picking Fury; with both fighters at their best, he has shown that his style should be enough to nullify Joshua's ferocity. Yet part of the intrigue and mystery of this fight is we just don't know how diminished either fighter's powers are. Daniel Dubois and Prenga have shown a fragility to Joshua, yet it remains to be seen how aggressive Fury's strategy will be and he has never presided over the division due to his power, which could encourage Joshua to engage more than he might otherwise, in a hypothetical rematch against a ferocious Dubois. This is all to say that my instinct takes me to Joshua's conditioning and how fading forces in this unforgiving sport usually cling onto that power and physicality when other weapons evade them.

Joshua, clearly, is one of the most freakish athletes the division and sport has ever seen. Right now he is in impeccable shape, with downright frightening conditioning, even if optics in boxing can be fool's gold. However, marry that with a desperation to seize closure in his career, a spiritual motivation from the tragic accident that robbed him of two close friends, I can see Joshua capturing the moment. Much like a prime Joshua showcased against Wladimir Klitschko, it would be naive to think Joshua won't have a scary moment or two, but he can rally, as evidenced even in his devastating defeat by Dubois, in which he briefly threatened a sensational comeback. Therefore I'm going for a Joshua stoppage in a fight littered with mistakes and openings, whereby a relentless AJ assault overwhelms an exhausted Fury.

Will Castle: The clock is ticking on both men, which means this is no longer a fight that will decide the best heavyweight in the world – or British heavyweight, at that – as it would have a few years ago. Their respective vulnerabilities, rather than their powers, are playing a greater part in shaping predictions, which says a lot. And in that regard, Joshua looks worse off. His Prenga return was a near-catastrophe and his chin seems to be all but gone, as demonstrated in that Daniel Dubois loss, which confirmed his drop in the British heavies hierarchy. While Fury didn't exactly sparkle on his fifth comeback from retirement, I back him to get the job done against his rival. My prediction sees Fury win it on points in a comfortable outing in the Cardiff cold, putting AJ down for good measure.

Luke Baker: If only this fight had happened five years ago... Instead we get these ageing, broken (mentally, as much as physically) versions of two of British boxing's most famous sons. But it's Joshua who looks much more vulnerable. The Prenga comeback fight was a disaster for him. He was brave to get back in the ring at all after the tragedy that befell him in Nigeria last December but would have lost if Prenga (an absolute nobody in boxing terms, remember) had been able to kick on after that two-knockdown first round. While AJ deserves credit for battling back from the brink to win it in round two, it all bodes very, very badly. There have always been questions over Joshua's chin and Fury still has the power to take advantage of that. He'll catch him early and that will be that. Fury to win by knockout in the first few rounds.

Michael Jones: A few years ago, when both fighters were in their prime, I would have given the edge to Joshua due to his superior firepower, but times have changed. Both Joshua and Fury have suffered high-profile defeats at the hands of Oleksandr Usyk and Joshua's defeat to Dubois in 2024 is the type of beating that's hard to recover from. As much as we'd like this fight to live up to the grudge match hype it'll be sold on, I see it being a more muted and tactical affair. The Gypsy King has shown he can take a hit, and I see him keeping Joshua at bay until the latter rounds before Fury takes the contest on points.

articles.title: Bill Simmons Proposes Blockbuster Nikola Jokic to Rockets Trade After Houston Gets Blown Out by Heat
articles.summary: After watching the Houston Rockets get blown out 128-110 in Miami on Monday, NBA analyst Bill Simmons proposed a blockbuster trade idea that would swap Alper...
articles.body:
After watching the Houston Rockets get blown out 128-110 in Miami on Monday, NBA analyst Bill Simmons proposed a blockbuster trade idea that would swap Alperen Sengun for Nikola Jokic.

Sengun is having a career year, averaging 22.8 points, 9.3 rebounds and 7.2 assists on 55.8% shooting, including 48.1% from 3 (stats before Wednesday's game against the Pacers). Although Houston only suffered its fourth loss this season against Miami, Simmons felt the team looked small. The analyst suggested a Jokic trade could resolve that.

"Miami really exposed them last night," he said on The Bill Simmons Podcast on Tuesday. "They just bullied them… I thought [Davion] Mitchell was too fast for Houston's guards. That was another issue. Giannis [Antetokounmpo] just overpowered them a few times. Houston was a team I had as a top-five contender. "They looked small last night. And there are too many teams that are big up front, and I think they really have to start wondering if they have the right people in place. And my question is, they have Brooklyn's first-rounder this year that they can swap. They also have Phoenix's first. They have a bunch of tradeable contracts – [Tari] Eason, [Reed] Sheppard, Jabari [Smith Jr.] and they have [Kevin] Durant at $43 million this year, $46 million next year. "Do they just make one play for Joker [Nikola Jokic]? And just see what Denver says? 'Cause they can put Sengun in that trade, they can put Sheppard… [Clint] Capela's expiring, swap picks, the Phoenix first."

Giannis [Antetokounmpo] just overpowered them a few times. Houston was a team I had as a top-five contender.

"They looked small last night. And there are too many teams that are big up front, and I think they really have to start wondering if they have the right people in place. And my question is, they have Brooklyn's first-rounder this year that they can swap. They also have Phoenix's first. They have a bunch of tradeable contracts – [Tari] Eason, [Reed] Sheppard, Jabari [Smith Jr.] and they have [Kevin] Durant at $43 million this year, $46 million next year.

"Do they just make one play for Joker [Nikola Jokic]? And just see what Denver says? 'Cause they can put Sengun in that trade, they can put Sheppard… [Clint] Capela's expiring, swap picks, the Phoenix first."

Simmons noted it would be a tremendous win-now move that would probably solve every offensive issue the Rockets have but do little for defense. However, Simmons feels the interior defense, even with the players available now, isn't that great, so it shouldn't matter.

Nikola Jokic has a player option next season and he hasn't signed an extension with the Nuggets. He's maintained that he wants to remain with Denver. However, as things stand, the Nuggets may not finish top six in the standings, and a championship dream seems far off amid a 7-5 run (before Wednesday's game against the Celtics).

If things don't improve and the Nuggets can't promise Jokic a better roster, teams will likely try to lure the three-time MVP away.

Nuggets are unlikely to trade Nikola Jokic

The Nuggets haven't had many generational players land on their roster. Nikola Jokic is the best they've had. Since they are a small-market team, have limited picks over the next few seasons and no prospects to develop, Denver is unlikely to cash in on Jokic.

Instead, the Nuggets might aggressively hunt roster upgrades by putting everyone else on the table to give Jokic another shot at a title. Denver has been reluctant to go over the second apron, which would increase its tax bill, but the front office hasn't hesitated to pull the trigger on major deals.

articles.title: Big 12 football tiebreakers: Utah, Texas Tech near conference title game
articles.summary: Three teams have the inside track to the Big 12 title game. Only two can make it. A look at the tiebreaker scenario with two games left for each team.
articles.body:
The Big 12 still counts seven teams in the mix for the its championship game: Utah, Texas Tech, Brigham Young, Baylor , Arizona, Arizona State and Houston.

Realistically, the race is down to just the Utes , Red Raiders and BYU, and the final pairing may be determined as soon as this weekend.

It's hard to picture a way that Utah falls short. The Utes are one of just two unbeaten teams in the Bowl Subdivision and have already defeated Houston, BYU and Arizona.

That puts the focus on the race for second place between Texas Tech and BYU. While a game behind the Red Raiders heading into Saturday, BYU still has a viable path to the title game. Just getting there might be enough to earn an at-large bid to the College Football Playoff given an earlier win against Notre Dame.

Here's how the Big 12 title pairing will be decided these next two weeks:

Contenders: Utah (7-0), Texas Tech (6-1), Brigham Young (5-2).

Utah can clinch its spot this weekend in one of two ways. The Utes are in with a win against TCU or a BYU loss at Kansas.

The only way Utah finishes outside the top two is by losing out while BYU wins out and Texas Tech loses to Baylor but beats TCU in the finale. That would leave the Utes in third because of a worse record than Tech and BYU in games against common conference competition.

Texas Tech is in a similar spot. The Red Raiders can clinch and earn a spot opposite Utah with a win against Baylor and a BYU loss. They can also clinch by winning out regardless of what the Cougars do.

BYU has a plausible scenario to reach the top two. It would finish in second with a clean finish and one loss by Texas Tech, since the Cougars would have a better record against common Big 12 competition.

The Big 12 will compete with the ACC to get a second team in the playoff. With Utah close to locking down a spot in the field, the league's most foolproof scenario for adding a second team would require the Utes to win out and then lose the title game to either the Texas Tech or BYU. Both the Red Raiders and Cougars would have an argument for an at-large bid by winning out and then losing a close game to the Utes for the conference title, but whether one would earn a bid hinges on helpful results in the other Power Four leagues.

articles.summary: Your daily San Francisco 49ers news for Thursday, November 19th, 2026
articles.body:
Elevation gain? 49ers hope for an edge vs. Vikings in Mexico City by getting expletives out early (paywall) "After arriving in Colorado Springs on Sunday night, the 49ers will spend a week in a high-elevation environment, which Fibel said is when the "partial benefits" of altitude acclimatization can start to be realized. Before kickoff, the 49ers will get through a rough stretch that often occurs during days 2 to 4 after arriving at a high altitude in which sleep is disrupted and fatigue and dehydration risk are common.

"By game time they will have had a chance to partly acclimate where they're not going to have as much as those deficits," said Fibel, who works at Cedars-Sinai Orthopaedics and Sports Medicine in Los Angeles. "Their sleep is more regulated and they're more adjusted to the decreased oxygen that's available as they're competing."

The Vikings will arrive Saturday — avoiding the negative delayed effects — after their extended elevation-room work at the team facility. Fibel noted elevation sessions can start to increase the body's ability to produce red blood cells, which can help transport oxygen.

"That can take several weeks to start happening," Fibel said. "So their approach gives them some of the benefits of the exposure to high altitude."

Fibel declined to say which approach he'd choose if he was running an NFL team, terming it a "challenging question" due to a variety of factors. For example, the Vikings will maintain their weekly routine by staying home while the 49ers are displaced during a nine-day trip that began Saturday in Dallas. However, the 49ers' weeklong exposure to high elevation could be more beneficial than the Vikings' multi-week elevation-room sessions."

Where the 49ers' biggest defensive concern is heading into the second half "The Raiders were 6-for-10 on late downs. They converted five in a row before the final two opportunities. The defense forced Dallas into an absurd number of late-down attempts —21, to be specific. You'd like to think that forcing 21 late-down attempts means you're doing something right defensively. However, only six of those were six yards and longer. The Niners allowed a 3-for-6 conversion rate on those, but one of those was converted on 4th & 1.

It's difficult to generate a pass rush in shorter yardage situations, since the quarterback can throw the ball quickly. You're putting more pressure on your coverage units. And, as we know, that is not a strong suit for the Niners….Morris had his work cut out for him heading into 2026. So far, he's done a good job of limiting the damage. The Niners have traded field goals for touchdowns. With their offense, it's a prudent approach. They're 11th in red zone scoring.

But as the schedule stiffens and offenses improve, we're starting to see cracks in the defense, enough that it's a concern as we head into the second half. It seems like the root of it all is failing to get off the field on late downs."

Kyle Shanahan shares 49ers injury updates and previews Vikings matchup "They've been good. We haven't been around the players much. They were away from us Monday and Tuesday after we reviewed the game from Dallas on Monday. Coaches, we've kind of just been in our hotel rooms and our offices just working, but I definitely am out of breath a little bit right now walking over here. Everyone does feel it just like you always do when you come to Colorado, but it'll be good to get out on the field today, get in the sun and get to work."

Kawakami Mailbag: Warriors emergency! Answers that might get fans mad! (Paywall) "Sacks sometimes happen in random and mysterious ways and right now none of them are happening for Bosa, who still is sitting on zero sacks this season (in four games) and went offside twice on Sunday.

I think it's fair to say that the 49ers need more from him, especially if they're not getting much from anybody rushing from the opposite side. But Bosa had four quarterback pressures on Sunday; sacks are likely coming.

He also is coming off of the third ACL surgery of his career. Who knows what physical percentage Bosa's playing at now? Maybe he won't come close to winning another Defensive Player of the Year or even get to double-digit sacks again, but I learned long ago that you can't measure a pass rusher by a handful of games against offenses that are concentrating on making sure he doesn't wreck things."

Florida basketball will look to close out its trip to Las Vegas on a positive note when the Gators play West Virginia on Thursday, Nov. 19.

The No. 1 Gators (5-1) dropped their first game of the season to Houston after falling 86-76 at the Players Era event on Wednesday, Nov. 18. UF knocked down 15 shots from beyond the arc, which included a 26-point performance by Denzel Aberdeen. However, Florida struggled to overcome its 12 turnovers and only attempted nine free throws compared to Houston's 27.

"We're not giving ourselves a real chance in those circumstances," Florida coach Todd Golden said. "It's frustrating to have a game where we make 15 threes.

"They get three times the amount of cracks at the (free) throw line as we do in a game where I think both teams were attacking the paint. Both teams were playing physically. Just didn't go our way that way today."

UF will now take on West Virginia (4-1) in the third-place game.

The Mountaineers opened the tournament with a 76-70 win over Auburn but dropped the semis matchup to Kansas 86-82. In that loss, freshman Miles Sadler scored 34 points.

articles.title: Vote for the PNJ girls basketball preseason player of the year
articles.summary: Voting for the PNJ girls basketball preseason player of the yea ris now open. Cast your vote for one of 11 nominees until 12 p.m. CT on Nov. 26.
articles.body:
On Nov. 18, the PNJ released a list of 20 high school girls basketball players to watch from the Pensacola area.

You'll notice we didn't rank them. We narrowed down the list to 11 nominees for preseason player of the year, and that's where readers come in. Vote now for the PNJ girls basketball preseason player of the year from now until 12 p.m. CT on Nov. 26.

Please not that this has no impact on postseason all-area awards, which are selected by the PNJ with input from local coaches.

PNJ Girls Basketball Preseason Player of the Year nominees

Amani Bartholomew, West Florida: Bartholomew was a bright spot on a struggling Jaguars team a year ago, averaging 13.4 points, 9.8 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 3.5 steals on her way to second team all-area honors. Unfortunately she'll miss the start of her senior campaign with a broken foot, but is trying to return before the end of the season.

Nylah Brooks, Booker T. Washington: The UWF commit helped form arguably the area's best backcourt with Jada Clardy for the 5A state champions, averaging 10.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 2.0 steals per game. With Clardy, the Wildcats will depend on Brooks more on and off the court as they navigate defending their state title.

Makenna Enfinger, Central: The 5'11 junior thrived as the Jaguars top option a year ago, averaging a team 14.0 points along with 5.5 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 2.0 steals per game. She stuffed the stat sheet with 23 points, seven rebounds and seven assists in the Jaguars season-openning 59-52 win over Rocky Bayou Christian on Nov. 17.

Loghan Goodwin, Milton: The 5'9 Goodwin was the Panthers go-to player as a junior, averaging 11.7 points and 6.0 rebounds per game on her way to second team all-area honors. This winter, she'll have to lead a team without a home gym or a consistent practice location after Milton high school's gym suffered severe roof damage from Hurricane Isaias.

Danielle Gulley, Pensacola Catholic: The junior guard made the Crusaders go last year as a sophomore. She led Catholic in points (11.6), rebounds (5.1) and steals per game (3.4) on her way to second team all-area honors.

Presley Hawthorne, Jay: The Royals' longtime floor general returns for her senior season. She averaged 9.1 points, 2.8 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 1.7 steals per game. while helping Jay advance to the state championship for the first time since 1996.

Jaleah Jones, Navarre: The junior has been an impact player for the Raiders since she stepped onto a varsity court. She averaged a 13.4 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game as Navarre went from 9-13 in 2024-25 to 22-5 and District 1-6A runner-up in 2025-26.

Aubreigh Nelson, Jay: Fresh off helping Jay win its first ever volleyball state championship , Nelson turns her attention to the hardwood. The senior averaged a team-high 13.7 points and 6.7 rebounds per game last year for a Royals squad that advanced to the state championship for the first time since 1996.

Leighton Osborn, Pace: The reigning PNJ Newcomer of the Year, Osborn moved from Roseburg, Oregon to the Panhandle and seamlessly transitioned to Florida high school basketball. She averaged 18.2 points and 6.9 rebounds per game, scoring in double figures in 21 of the Patriots 25 games and at least 20 points in 12 games.

Chioma Patterson, Pensacola: Simply put, Patterson is a matchup nightmare. The senior averaged 16.3 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 steals and 2.1 blocks per game as a junior, garnering first team all-area honors under longtime PHS head coach Allison Davis.

Olivia Pearce, L.E.A.D. Academy: The 6'3 Pierce was a force down low for the Lions last year, averaging 14.0 points, 10.4 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game on her way to second team all-area honors. The Lions will need more from Pierce this fall, especially with Burkett transferring to Pace.

articles.title: Holy Trinity, Merritt Island, Eau Gallie, MCC eye regional finals
articles.summary: Holy Trinity, Merritt Island, Eau Gallie and Melbourne Central Catholic compete for spots into a regional final.
articles.body:
Four Brevard County teams remain in the state football playoffs with the regional semifinals kicking off on Nov. 20 and continuing on Nov. 21.

Merritt Island and Eau Gallie host regional semifinals on Nov. 20 as a win by both schools would put them on a collision course for the regional final. Melbourne Central Catholic heads north to Jacksonville to take on top-seed Trinity Christian Academy looking to pull off the upset.

After weather forced the game to move back two days, Holy Trinity hosts Central Florida Christian Academy on Nov. 21 in the Independent League Pool B regional semifinals looking to make history.

Here's a preview of the four regional semifinals.

(4) Melbourne Central Catholic (8-2) at (1) Trinity Christian Academy (7-4), 7 p.m.

Melbourne Central Catholic seeks its first regional final in three years when it heads to top seed Trinity Christian Academy.

The Hustlers defeated Williston 38-6 in the first round of the state playoffs as the defense limited Williston to 145 total yards. MCC junior Will Warren posted his fourth game of at least 16 tackles as he hit that mark against the Mighty Red Devils to go with three tackles for loss and one sack.

Hustlers senior Noah Flores and junior Ryan Kling intercepted one pass. Sophomore Beckett Pinnick and senior Ty Goetsch matched Warren with three tackles for loss. Pinnick recorded eight tackles.

Offensively, sophomore Trenton Washington completed 18-of-26 passes for 301 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in his first career playoff start.

Hustlers senior Grady Bonenberger caught four passes for 148 yards and two touchdowns. Junior Cayden Varis received a 20-yard touchdown reception and ran for an 8-yard score. Flores gained 42 yards on the ground and scored on a 23-yard run.

Trinity Christian Academy enters the game on a four-game winning streak. It suffered three one-possession defeats, including a pair of overtime losses to ED White and American Heritage (Plantation).

The Conquerors shut out Father Lopez 41-0 in the regional quarterfinals. Entering the state playoffs, they rushed for 2,052 yards as a team with five rushers at least 196 yards.

TCA senior Hicks Zarah carried the ball 80 times for 451 yards and six touchdowns. Junior Terel Dallas finished with 442 yards and four touchdowns. Dallas threw 978 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions. His favorite target is junior Dylan Richards with 28 receptions, 444 yards and four touchdowns.

The Conquerors defense recorded 20 takeaways and 28 sacks during the regular season. Junior William Striglers led the team with 89 tackles and 12 tackles for loss. Trinity Christian junior Edgerrin Wells posted five sacks followed by four from Striglers and senior Jeremiah Desir.

Junior Zakhari Green is tied for eighth in the state with six interceptions. Seniors Terrell Pinkney and Dereious Williams recovered two fumbles.

(4) Santa Fe (9-2) at (1) Merritt Island (11-0), 7:30 p.m.

Merritt Island seeks its first regional final appearance in five years when it hosts Santa Fe. The Mustangs are coming off a 63-0 rout of Tenoroc in the regional quarterfinals as they scored 49 points in the first half.

Mustangs senior Kevin Verpaele tallied 170 yards and three touchdowns on 13-of-15 passing. Senior DeShaun Thomas and sophomore Elijah Mitchell combined for 12 receptions, 134 yards and three touchdowns. Senior Drew Sarver and sophomore Noah Smith caught one touchdown each. Junior Zaylan Chapple rushed for two touchdowns on three carries.

Merritt Island junior Amarri Hamilton posted five tackles, two tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks. Senior Kamar Fielder returned an interception 30 yards to the end zone. Senior Tory Love and sophomore Chase Akridge recovered a fumble.

Santa Fe avenged its regular season defeat to Dunnellon in the regional quarterfinals with a 35-7 win. The Raiders rushed for 269 yards led by senior Jasiah Powell's 119 yards and three touchdowns on 23 carries. Senior Jadathan Bryant gained 91 yards and one touchdown and junior Gavin Peterson also scored one touchdown coupled with 57 rushing yards.

Through Week 10 of the regular season, Santa Fe recorded 17.5 sacks, six interceptions and six fumble recoveries. Raiders senior Mason Nipper posted a team-high five sacks followed by four from senior Andrew Akins. Junior Elon James and senior Christian Barjon intercepted one pass and recovered one fumble.

(3) The Villages Charter (11-0) at (2) Eau Gallie (7-4), 7:30 p.m.

Eau Gallie took care of business at home in the regional quarterfinals defeating Titusville for the second time this season with a 25-10 win. It plays for its third-straight regional final berth.

After allowing the game's first touchdown, Eau Gallie held Titusville to three points on the next five drives. Senior Kayden Jaquez posted a team-high 10 tackles followed by six tackles from senior Amari Oquendo and Isaiah Danclair. Senior Zay Floyd recovered one fumble.

It was an efficient Commodores offense with 291 yards and four touchdowns on 40 plays. Senior Joseph Allen completed 11-of-14 passes for 158 yards and three touchdowns. Junior Zay Hawkins caught four passes for 64 yards and two touchdowns. Junior Troy Silberzahn hauled in a 3-yard touchdown.

On the ground, senior Donovan Richardson posted 16 rushes for 79 yards and one touchdown. Hawkins added 34 yards.

The Villages Charter, which moved up to Class 3A this season, recorded its first undefeated regular season and regional semifinal appearance in five years. The Buffalo defeated South Sumter 42-7 in the first round of the playoffs behind 419 total yards, five sacks and three takeaways.

Buffalo senior Jadence Kennedy completed 13-of-16 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns. Kennedy tossed a 64-yard touchdown to senior Tranard Roberts, a 49-yard touchdown to senior Bryce Norflee and one touchdown to senior Ja'Marian Clark who finished with three catches for 53 yards. Roberts rushed for a team-high 122 yards and one touchdown.

The Villages Charter senior Dominic Lopez and sophomore Maguire Mellinger posted a dozen tackles in the playoff win followed by 11 tackles from junior Zion Reed Jr. Juniors Jonathan Williams and Richard Jackson recorded two sacks. Senior Blake Branham intercepted one pass. Lopez and sophomore DJ Bryant tallied one fumble recovery.

(5) Central Florida Christian Academy (8-2) at (1) Holy Trinity (8-2), 5 p.m.

Holy Trinity, coming off its first postseason win in five years, looks to make history with a win and advance to its first regional final in school history. The Tigers are 0-10 all-time in the regional semifinals.

Holy Trinity ran away from Foundation Academy in the regional quarterfinals, scoring the final 35 points in a 45-6 win. The Tigers finished with 164 passing yards and 159 rushing yards.

Five different Tigers scored touchdowns. Sophomore Jackson Mobley completed 14-of-20 passes for 164 yards and three touchdowns. Juniors Hayden Argo, Aaron Raines and Zach Curran caught touchdowns. Sophomore Jacorey Mills posted 85 yards and one touchdown and freshman Michael Jackson finished with 67 yards and one touchdown.

Holy Trinity senior Omari Savage intercepted two passes, including returning one for a 78-yard touchdown. For the sixth time this season, the Tigers held an opponent to under 10 points.

Central Florida Christian Academy, playing its first FHSAA season since 2011, won its first FHSAA state playoff game in school history in the regional quarterfinals at Orangewood Christian.

The Eagles won 18-10 by scoring one touchdown in each of the final three quarters. Defensively, they forced three turnovers with one interception and two fumble recoveries and recorded 8.5 sacks.

CFCA senior Jondell Cennett recorded 14 tackles, 2.5 tackles and one sack. Eagles senior James Dorval Jr. and Yuarik Torres produced 2.5 sacks each. Senior Deshaun Jones finished with one interception and one fumble recovery.

Eagles freshman Gavin Pritzkau threw for 226 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions. Jones finished with seven receptions for 80 yards and one touchdown. Senior Melvin Mack recorded 6 catches for 77 yards and one touchdown.

articles.title: Like a Swiss Army knife, Nash Evans brings versatility to Clear Fork
articles.summary: Kicking, punting, returning? Catching passes, rushing, and playing defense? Exhausting, right? That's just a typical Friday night for Nash Evans.
articles.body:
BELLVILLE — Friday night's for Nash Evans are exhausting.

The Clear Fork senior starts games either lining up to kickoff or back deep to receive. If the Colts are on offense, he's out wide ready to catch passes or run a jet sweep and if they're on defense, he's lined up opposite a receiver or deep in the secondary depending on the play. And when they score, he doesn't even need to leave the field becuase he's kicking the extra point. On the off chance a drive stalls ... you guessed it, Evans is lined up deep to punt.

"Sometimes I get a sub maybe a couple times a game," Evans said. "But (realistically) I'm never not on the field."

It's just a testament to the level of trust his coaches, and temamates, have in him.

"With me doing everything, it comes with a lot of responsibility," Evans said. "Kicking, punting, returning, wide receiver, corner — there's a lot of responsibilites in those positions. Kicking, you have to get the extra point every time or else you're down one. I think my team definitely trusts me to do that, my coaches trust me, and I'm proficient in everything I do.

"But they trust me to do whatever they need."

That's a blessing, and a curse, for the Colts.

"He's a great athlete who can do a lot of different things, but he also draws a lot of eyeballs," Clear Fork coach Aaron Brokaw said. "There have been weeks where I'm sure it has been frustrating for him because it has been frustrating for us that we weren't able tot get him the number of touches we wanted to because opposing defenses pay so much attention to him. But other weeks when other guys have had big weeks, they start to take their eyes away from him a little bit and it's easier to get him back into the floodgates.

Clear Fork's success this season undoubtedly has been a team effort, but it's because the team has guys with versatility. But there are very few players on the gridiron anywhere with Evans' high level of versatility.

Through 12 games this season he has caught 22 passes for 356 yards and four touchdowns, logged 27 carries for 247 yards and two touchdowns, recorded 28 tackles with two interceptions on defense, made 43-of-45 extra points attempted, successfully made 3-of-8 field goals with a long of 40 yards, averaged 35.4 yards on 25 punts with seven inside the 20 and returned six kicks for 110 yards.

"It's a really tough spot to be in if you're a free safety ... being able to run the ball then go hard play action over the top to a guy with Nash's speed and catch radius," Brokaw said. "He had six catches last week but three of them were pretty heavily contsted and he fought for the ball to come down with it. It's not just that he's wide open, he's also a very talented receiver.

"(And) he has been pretty solid with extra points ... we've gotten some field goal attempts we wouldn't have had in years past because of his leg. Some of them have been good, others — like Friday night — he kicked the tee further than the ball went. But we trust him up to about 45."

Pretty impressive considering Evans just recently started kicking in his football career.

"I didn't start kicking until junior year," he said. "I punted a little bit freshman and sophomore year, but I wasn't really a kicker. I was on kick return, and sophomore year I was just a corner and safety, I didn't play offense. Junior year came and I showed up and proved I could play everything."

His success this season is largely in part due to Evans, and the rest of the senior class, taking their lumps the last few years.

"A lot of these guys as freshmen — especially as sophomores — we were having to put out there in positions they physically weren't quite ready for yet, but we knew it was going to be a good experience for them in the long term," Brokaw said. "To their credit, they rose to the occasion and probably passed the (benchmark) we had for a lot of them."

Coincidentally, it was the year Brokaw took over the program.

"The culture built over time, we've slowly gotten more wins and built this team together," Evans said. "My freshman year it was like everyone was giving up because of a new coach, they wanted to just be over with it.

"It was all underclassmen that were wanting to put in the work and play the game."

Those underclassmen are now seniors preparing to play the biggest game of their lives — a Division IV, Region 14 championship against rival Shelby on Friday night, Nov. 20, at Arlin Field.

articles.title: Charles Leclerc responds to British journalist’s three-word insult after F1 ban
articles.summary: A seasoned Formula 1 journalist had his accreditation revoked for the rest of the season after his article about Leclerc
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc says he was surprised by the "choice of words" after being branded a "sneaky little bastard" by a British journalist, who has since been banned from the paddock.

Seasoned F1 journalist Jonathan McEvoy, who works for the Daily Mail , had his accreditation revoked last week for the final three races of the 2026 season after the FIA took action for his language in a piece criticising Ferrari driver Leclerc for his part in a clash with Lewis Hamilton in Mexico City.

The Mail have since insisted they will not cover any Formula 1 for the rest of the season, calling the removal of accreditation "an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the press." McEvoy also blamed Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur for the situation, calling him a "tubby little nobody."

Leclerc, speaking ahead of this weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix , refused to comment on the sanction but did respond to the article itself.

"I saw the article, and I was quite surprised by the choice of words, but apart from that, I don't have much to say," Leclerc said.

"Obviously, the sanction is not up to me, and I do believe that we are in a position where there are a lot of critics, which is completely normal.

"I think the job of a journalist is to ask not-so-nice questions and to do the not-so-nice articles as well sometimes. I was quite surprised by the choice of words when I saw the article, and on the sanction itself, I've got absolutely nothing to do with it.

"I don't have much to say about it, and the only thing I will say is that, as Formula 1 drivers, I think we are used to not this kind of criticism, but to criticism in general and to critics.

"It is definitely the job of journalists to ask the bad questions and do some tough headlines, but I was surprised by the choice of words."

Leclerc is currently fifth in the championship standings, 12 points off Hamilton with three rounds remaining.

Ferrari, meanwhile, are second in the constructors' championship and cannot catch Mercedes, who were crowned champions at the last race in Brazil.
