articles.title: Vincent Kompany provides health update ahead of his first Bayern match since collapse
articles.summary: Kompany collapsed during training on 23 October and was treated for meningeal irritation
articles.body:
Vincent Kompany says he is back in "very good health" as he prepares to make his return to the Bayern Munich dugout for the first time since collapsing at training .

Kompany was hospitalised after collapsing at a reserve team training session on 23 October and was diagnosed with meningeal irritation , an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

He missed five Bayern games as the club prioritised his health, with assistant coach Aaron Danks taking the reins and going unbeaten during that period.

But after returning to the club's training ground during the international break, Kompany is raring to make his managerial comeback and take charge of his first game since drawing 2-2 with Arsenal a month ago.

"I was grateful for the support," Kompany said. "It was very intense. At the time, it was a new experience. Looking back, everything went perfectly.

"I received immediate support from the club and from the doctors. I'm very grateful.

"I'm in very good health. We've done lots of tests, all of which have come back clear."

The Belgian was sporting a sling on his left arm after injuring his shoulder during the collapse.

Kompany said the incident prompted him to think differently about his health and that he "perhaps didn't listen closely" enough to his body when he returned for the Arsenal game despite having battled a viral infection that week.

Nevertheless, he revealed he had fun watching his team from a "fascinating" new perspective as Danks took charge, and claimed that Bayern's 2-0 win over Atletico Madrid earlier this month "was one of the finest moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn't there".

"I'm coming off the longest holidays I ever had, it's been the longest international break I ever had," Kompany said. "It happened, it can happen to everyone, but you can learn from it."

His first game back sees Bayern take on Koln on Friday evening, with the club top of the Bundesliga - ahead of Borussia Dortmund on goal difference.

articles.title: A Glasgow hero turns 85: Happy birthday, Theo Redder!
articles.summary: In 1961, the Werl-born player moved from SC Preußen Werl to Borussia Dortmund and developed into a defender of international calibre. Speaking about his foot...
articles.body:
In 1961, the Werl-born player moved from SC Preußen Werl to Borussia Dortmund and developed into a defender of international calibre. Speaking about his footballing qualities, Redder said: "My strengths were being tough on myself and on others too. I really got stuck in. And my pace. And I could play a bit of football as well."

With BVB, he won the German championship in 1963 and the DFB-Pokal in 1965. His greatest triumph followed in Glasgow in 1966. Facing favourites Liverpool FC in the European Cup Winners' Cup final, Borussia first had to weather a difficult opening spell. Redder also helped out on the goal line: "We had a bit of luck there too. One hit me on the knee right on the line." With a 2–1 victory after extra time, BVB became the first German club to win a European trophy.

"You can't describe it. It's only afterwards that you realise what you've achieved," Redder recalled of the moments after the final whistle at Hampden Park. The celebrations, the lap of honour with the trophy and the subsequent welcome in Dortmund remain unforgettable: "Through the city in open-top cars. That was something special."

Redder made 115 Bundesliga appearances and played 16 European matches for the Black and Yellows. He also won one cap for the German national team. A torn muscle marked the beginning of the far-too-early end to his playing career. "I was never again the Theo Redder I had been in the years before," he said of the injury's consequences. When his father became seriously ill, he returned home. He qualified as a master baker and took over his parents' bakery.

His close relationship with Borussia outlasted his playing career. For around two decades, Redder ran the club's legends team, kept in touch with his former teammates and remains a member of the Council of Elders to this day. BVB was "a kind of family" to him, he said. He added: "Borussia also means a piece of home to me."

articles.title: “Massive Overpay” – Fans React As Twins Sign 37-Year-Old All-Star on $55M Free Agent Contract
articles.summary: The Minnesota Twins have signed veteran ace Sonny Gray to a two-year, $55 million deal, according to multiple MLB analysts, including Jon Heyman of the New Y...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Twins have signed veteran ace Sonny Gray to a two-year, $55 million deal, according to multiple MLB analysts, including Jon Heyman of the New York Post. Heyman reports that the 37-year-old right-hander will earn $20 million in 2027, with a 2028 player option that carries a $5 million buyout or a $30 million salary.

The deal also includes a mutual option for 2029, with a $5 million buyout or a $27.5 million salary. Finally, the contract includes an opt-out after the first year and full no-trade clauses. Since the blockbuster deal was announced, fans have taken to social media to share their blunt reactions.

Gray joins the Twins after declining his $30 million mutual option for 2027 and accepting a $10 million buyout from Boston. He spent the 2026 season with the Red Sox, posting outstanding numbers : an AL-leading 18-5 record, a 2.72 ERA, 149 strikeouts, and a 1.15 WHIP in 29 starts. Gray finished fifth in the 2026 AL Cy Young voting.

It's his second stint in Minnesota , where he joins a deep rotation featuring veteran starters Pablo López, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley, Bailey Ober, and Dean Kremer, along with farm system prospects Connor Prielipp, Zebby Matthews, and Mick Abel.

Twins Announce Star Signings on Back-to-Back Days

After bolstering its starting rotation with Gray, Minnesota made another positive announcement Tuesday: catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer to return in 2027. The two deals reaffirm an earlier remark by team chairman Tom Pohlad that the franchise will make "meaningful investments" in payroll this offseason.

The Twins need at least one more bat to strengthen their lineup. However, this year's free-agent class lacks credible hitters beyond several outfielders, and Minnesota already has a surplus of influential players who can play outfield defense. So, it will be interesting to see the ballclub's next move this offseason.

articles.title: Lions CB D.J. Reed: 'I don't want to rush' return from hip injury
articles.summary: D.J. Reed is expected to miss his third straight game this week with a hip injury he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
In hindsight, D.J. Reed probably came back too early from the hamstring strain he suffered last season. And now that he's over the initial frustration of having to miss more time with a hip injury, the Detroit Lions' No. 1 cornerback is being careful not to make that mistake again.

"I definitely want to make sure I come back and I feel like myself," Reed said Wednesday, Nov. 18. "I don't want to rush it especially cause our defense is playing well so I don't want to be a hindrance. So I just got to be honest with myself and be honest with the trainers and my coaches to see if I'm ready to go, whenever that is."

Reed has not played since injuring his hip on a key fourth-and-5 pass breakup in the fourth quarter of the Lions ' Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . He said he likely will miss his third straight game Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Last year, Reed was playing good football when he hurt his hamstring in a September game against the Cleveland Browns. He was diagnosed with a Grade II/ III strain , missed six weeks, then struggled upon his return.

That experience has colored Reed's conservative approach to his current rehab. He said he doesn't expect to spend time on injured reserve, but called his return date "up in the air."

"When you get hurt you obviously want to get back on the field as soon as possible," Reed said. "But I kind of [underestimated] the severity of a hamstring strain, especially a high-grade one, cause I never hurt my hamstring that bad. So in hindsight, yes, I do feel like I came back early. So dealing with this right here, I just definitely want to make sure I definitely come back confident, healthy and ready to play compared to coming back and not being myself. That's not smart, that's not helping the team."

The Lions (7-2) have won five straight and have gotten improved play from their secondary in recent weeks.

Roger McCreary and Rock Ya-Sin played most of the game at corner in last week's win over the New England Patriots. Khalil Dorsey, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Nick Whiteside also are in the rotation at cornerback. And All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is expected to make his long-awaited return from a knee injury Sunday.

Reed, who got off to a rocky start to this season, allowed just six catches for 41 yards on 14 pass targets in the three games before he got hurt.

He said he needs to regain his burst and top-end speed in training before he's ready to return to action.

"Everything's in the air right now so we're just trying to hit top-end speeds, trying to make sure that I can run and make sure that I can cover and stay in front of people without it hurting, without it pulling," he said. "Kind of just going day-by-day, so it's kind of in the air."

Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com . Follow him on Bluesky , X and Instagram at @davebirkett.

articles.title: ‘That little empty space is for us’: CSY boys ready for banner season
articles.summary: CSY boys basketball brings back its entire varsity roster this season. The veteran squad is eyeing a district championship.
articles.body:
For the Christian School of York boys' basketball program, the blank space on the gymnasium wall is more than just empty drywall — it is a daily reminder of unfinished business.

Sitting right beside the school's recent back-to-back District 3 championship baseball banners, that open spot represents the Defenders' primary goal this winter: capturing a Commonwealth Christian Athletic Conference (CCAC) title and snapping a District 3 playoff drought that stretches back to 1991.

If the team's veteran core has its way, that space won't remain empty for long.

After graduating zero seniors from last year's 13-9 squad, CSY returns its entire varsity roster, bringing three to four years of varsity experience and tightly knit team chemistry to the hardwood. For a senior class that endured a 2-20 campaign as freshmen — inheriting a program that had previously lost 102 consecutive games over seven years — this season marks the culmination of a ground-up rebuild.

"These guys kept their heads up. They played hard. They kept getting better," head coach John Zerfing said of a group led by Austin Holbritter, Parker Tyler, and Colt Zerfing. "And now, I feel like this year, they're going to reap the benefits of all that developmental work."

That motivation is fueled heavily by how last season ended. Sitting at the No. 11 spot in the district rankings — just outside the 10-team cutoff — CSY had a late-season road game added to its schedule against Lancaster County Christian School immediately following a league playoff contest. Forced to travel 90 minutes and play on back-to-back nights, the Defenders fell in overtime, abruptly ending their postseason hopes.

"We're coming for them," Holbritter said of the rematch with LCCS, which is circled on the calendar for Jan. 5 at home.

To get over the hump, CSY is leaning into its identity as the Defenders — a moniker the school adopted when transitioning away from the Crusaders. The coaching staff is emphasizing relentless defensive pressure designed to spark an up-tempo transition offense.

While Tyler previously shouldered much of the offensive creation, the Defenders boast a balanced attack where all five starters can score. Players have dedicated the offseason to open-gym workouts, building strength, and expanding their offensive skill sets — including Holbritter, whose improved shooting and two-way versatility have stood out to his teammates.

"Last year I felt like Parker was our main guy, he was creating everything for us, and this year I feel like we have more than that," Holbritter noted. "We have other people that can drive to the paint, kick out, get better shots, and just create more offense for everyone."

CSY will face a revamped CCAC landscape this winter. The 16-team conference has dissolved its East-West divisions into a single unified standings table, meaning the Defenders will play 15 league games — facing every conference opponent once, including unfamiliar eastern foes like Linville Hill, Coventry Christian, High Point, and Conestoga Christian.

The Defenders officially open practice Nov. 20 before tipping off their season Dec. 4 at the Harrisburg Christian tournament. With a multi-sport roster of proven winners — including several members of the championship baseball squad — CSY is ready to turn years of hard lessons into hardware.

"There's a little spot right there," assistant coach Eric Tyler said of the gym wall. "That little empty space is for us."

articles.title: South Africa beats Bangladesh on Day 5 of first cricket test after Harmer shines again
articles.summary: JOHANNESBURG (AP) — Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first test by nine wickets on Thu...
articles.body:
JOHANNESBURG (AP) — Simon Harmer ran through Bangladesh's tail and South Africa knocked off the 12 runs required to win the first test by nine wickets on Thursday, taking a 1-0 lead in the teams' two-match cricket test series.

Resuming on 100-5 at the Wanderers, Bangladesh's lower-order batters couldn't handle the off-spin of Harmer, who took four of the five wickets to help dismiss the tourists for 168 and revive memories of taking 6-16 on Day 5 of the series-clinching victory over Australia last month.

The Proteas lost first-innings century-maker Marques Ackerman — for a second-ball duck — on the way to reaching their target before lunch, at 12-1. Soon after getting bowled off a no-ball, Aiden Markram (8 not out) scored the winning run.

South Africa dethroned Australia for the top spot in the ICC test team rankings with that series win last month and is the reigning world test champion.

articles.title: Brendon McCullum vows that England will not rush Jacob Bethell return
articles.summary: Bethell flew home from the white-ball tour of Australia as his planned comeback was scuppered
articles.body:
Brendon McCullum admits England need to be careful with their future handling of Jacob Bethell , as he undergoes a second bout of knee surgery .

Bethell, 23, was cast as English cricket's 'star boy' following his fine Ashes century in Sydney at the turn of the year, having already become the country's youngest ever men's captain during a T20 series against Ireland last autumn.

But his summer ground to a halt when he suffered a right knee injury against India in July, a setback that was initially expected to keep him sidelined for just three to four weeks.

In reality it has proved a more significant problem and an initial operation has been unable to solve the issue and he will go back under the knife on Thursday.

He flew home from the ongoing white-ball tour of Australia , scuppering a planned comeback and raising question marks over when he may be cleared for duty.

Uncertainty over his fitness played a part in his release by IPL franchise Royal Challengers Bangalore , and it is possible he could miss all six of England's winter Tests in South Africa, Bangladesh and Melbourne.

Limited-overs head coach McCullum, who spent time with Bethell in Perth before he flew home for consultations with a specialist, believes it is now imperative to give Bethell time to make a full recovery rather than rush him back to action.

"He's like a young colt… only the good ones get injured," he said.

"He's one of those guys we are going to have to look after, manage him and make sure we do the right thing by him. He's going to have a long and successful career and if that means we have to take things a bit slower in the first steps of it then we will do so.

"He's an incredibly valuable player for English cricket over the next decade or so and it's worth taking our time with it."

McCullum's side completed a 2-1 ODI series win over Australia on Wednesday, and move quickly into a five-match T20 leg which begins at the MCG on Friday.

Test players Joe Root, Ben Duckett, Jofra Archer, Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson have all departed to prepare for the trip to South Africa, leaving fresh faces including 18-year-old Thomas Rew, Eddie Jack, James Coles and Henry Crocombe to take the strain.

But perhaps it is the status of the team's oldest player, 38-year-old Adil Rashid, which continues to generate most intrigue.

Rashid appears to have lost his long-held role as first-choice white-ball spinner to Liam Dawson in recent weeks and McCullum stopped short of promising he would return to the 20-over side.

"The problem is not that he isn't playing well, it's that sometimes you only have room for one spinner, and that's been Daws," he said.

"We have to look at conditions and opposition and pick the team that gives the best chance of winning and we will have those conversations.

"Daws has really put his hand up and performed. He's done brilliantly since coming in but that is no slight on Rash.

"Naturally, all players are disappointed when they miss out but Rash is a team player."

images.caption: Liam Dawson, right, has been keeping Adil Rashid out of the England one-day team (James Ross/AP)

articles.title: Texas A&M sophomore WR is 'questionable' before facing Oklahoma
articles.summary: Texas A&M sophomore WR TK Norman is listed as "questionable" with a 50% chance to play against Oklahoma on Saturday.
articles.body:
Texas A&M sits at 4-6 and 1-6 in SEC play after falling to Tennessee 22-7 in Week 11, while Oklahoma is riding a two-game winning streak after defeating a ranked Ole Miss team at home on Sunday afternoon. While the Sooners have found more success, I don't expect a blowout, given both teams' offensive struggles.

After producing just 179 yards against the Volunteers, including 71 passing yards and an interception from senior quarterback Marcel Reed, first-year offensive coordinator Holmon Wiggins is on track to be fired this offseason, while third-year head coach Mike Elko is dealing with plenty of pressure, especially after AD Trev Alberts departed for the same job with Michigan after just two years.

While Holmon Wiggins' bland scheme deserves at least 50% of the blame for Texas A&M's offensive woes, Mike Elko's decision to continue starting Marcel Reed has resulted in little to no improvement in the passing game, but to give credit where credit is due, several wide receivers have stood out, including sophomore TK Norman.

After Mike Elko stated on Monday that Norman , who has reeled in 15 receptions for 226 yards, could miss Saturday's game, the sophomore was listed as questionable with a 50% chance to play against Oklahoma. Aside from sophomore DT Landon Rink being listed as out for the matchup, Norman is the only new addition to the first injury report.

Texas A&M will face Oklahoma on Saturday at 2:45 p.m. on ESPN2.

Contact/Follow us @AggiesWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Texas A&M news, notes and opinions. Follow Cameron on X: @CameronOhnysty .

articles.title: Five return for Wales' World Cup play-off final
articles.summary: Ceri Holland is in the Wales squad for next month's Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway despite being out since September through injury.
articles.body:
Ceri Holland has been named in the Wales squad for next month's Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway despite being out since September through injury.

Olivia Clark, Hayley Ladd, Rhiannon Roberts and Ella Powell are also included after fitness issues, but Ffion Morgan, Laura Hughes and Scarlett Hill are among those who miss out with injuries.

The versatile Holland, arguably Wales' most influential player, has been out with a muscle problem, though she is thought to be close to returning to action for club side Liverpool.

Her involvement is a major boost for Wales as they attempt to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time.

Rhian Wilkinson's side face Norway at the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Leicester goalkeeper Clark and Sunderland defender Roberts are also included even though they have not played since September, but the loss of promising Manchester United defender Hill is a blow given her impressive displays against Albania.

Crystal Palace's Ladd and Powell, of Bristol City, have played for their clubs since missing Wales' World Cup play-off semi-final games against the Albanians last month.

Winger Morgan had returned to action for West Ham after not being involved against Albania, but she is back on the sidelines after getting injured while playing for the Hammers last weekend.

Like Southampton midfielder Hughes, Mia Ross – who is without a club after leaving Charlton in September - is missing again, while Fulham full-back Charlie Estcourt is another absentee.

There is also no place for Sunderland defender Tara Bourne, who has switched allegiance from England to Wales but is injured.

There is a recall for once-capped teenager Gwen Zimmerman, who plays for American side Northwestern NCAA, while Newcastle youngster Casi Gregson is included again after winning her first cap against Albania.

Wolves midfielder Chloe Williams keeps her place having been a late call-up for the semi-final, while the only uncapped player in the squad is third-choice goalkeeper Soffia Kelly.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway may not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

Olivia Clark (Leicester City), Soffia Kelly (Aston Villa), Safia Middleton-Patel (Watford – on loan from Manchester United), Hannah Cain (Everton), Mayzee Davies (Manchester City), Gemma Evans (Newcastle United), Olivia Francis (Wolverhampton Wanderers), Casi Gregson (Newcastle United), Mared Griffiths (Manchester United), Ceri Holland (Liverpool), Elise Hughes (Sunderland), Sophie Ingle (Bristol City), Angharad James (Seattle Reign), Lois Joel (Newcastle United), Carrie Jones (IFK Norrkoping), Hayley Ladd (Crystal Palace), Esther Morgan (Bristol City), Mary McAteer (Ipswich Town – on loan from Charlton Athletic), Phoebie Poole (Watford), Ella Powell (Bristol City), Rhiannon Roberts (Sunderland), Rachel Rowe (Nottingham Forest), Tianna Teisar (Watford), Lily Woodham (Liverpool), Chloe Williams (Wolverhampton Wanderers), Gwen Zimmerman (Northwestern NCAA).

images.caption: With 204 caps between them, Hayley Ladd (left) and Rhiannon Roberts (right) bring welcome experience to Wales' squad [FAW]

articles.title: Nou Mestalla: así diseña Daplast el 'seating' de un estadio para 70.000 espectadores
articles.standfirst: El Valencia CF aspira a triplicar los ingresos de su estadio con un recinto en el que cada detalle cuenta
articles.summary: El Valencia CF aspira a triplicar los ingresos de su estadio con un recinto en el que cada detalle cuenta
articles.body: Cuando los aficionados del Valencia CF estrenen el Nou Mestalla, encontrarán un estadio en el que hasta los detalles más cotidianos se han diseñado al milímetro. La distancia entre localidades, la altura de los respaldos o el espacio disponible para circular por las gradas forman parte de un proyecto con el que la entidad aspira a triplicar los ingresos directos de su estadio. El club valencianista, que prevé estrenar su nuevo recinto en el verano de 2027, quiere que el Nou Mestalla tenga actividad más allá del calendario de partidos, una exigencia que también influye en la elección de sus instalaciones y equipamientos. “Nuestro estadio está pensado para los 365 días del año, no sólo para los matchdays”, explica a 2Playbook Javier Solís, director general del Valencia CF. Entre esas decisiones figura el equipamiento de las gradas, donde el diseño de los asientos influye directamente en la comodidad, el espacio disponible y la circulación de los espectadores. Para este trabajo, el Valencia CF cuenta con Daplast, fabricante cordobés especializado en asientos para estadios y Stadium Partner del Nou Mestalla. La ingeniería detrás de 69.000 asientos La participación de Daplast en el Nou Mestalla comenzó mucho antes de la fabricación de los asientos. Como Stadium Partner, la compañía ha trabajado junto al Valencia CF desde la fase de diseño, con su oficina técnica implicada en la definición de las soluciones de seating, la distribución de localidades y la optimización del aforo. Este trabajo de ingeniería también ha incluido la adaptación de los modelos y el desarrollo de sistemas de fijación específicos para las características de las gradas. A partir de ese desarrollo técnico, Daplast asume la fabricación, logística e instalación de más de 69.000 asientos. El proceso se completará con la colocación y numeración de cada localidad, en coordinación con el avance de las obras del estadio. “En un proyecto de esta magnitud, intervienen muchas variables y cualquier decisión en una fase puede tener consecuencias en las siguientes”, señala Rafael Pérez-Esparza, CEO de Daplast. Esta coordinación será especialmente importante durante la instalación, que deberá acompasarse con el avance de las obras del estadio. Los trabajos de ingeniería y definición de modelos han ocupado buena parte de 2026. Tras esta fase, Daplast ha iniciado la fabricación en su planta de Córdoba, con la previsión de cerrar el año con alrededor de 10.000 asientos preparados para su instalación. Los trabajos en el estadio comenzarán en diciembre y se prolongarán hasta el próximo verano. El modelo Avatar será la solución principal para las gradas de Aforo General. Frente a los asientos monobloque del actual Mestalla, el nuevo estadio incorporará un modelo abatible cuyo fondo se reduce a 20 centímetros cuando está cerrado. Esta configuración libera espacio entre filas y facilita la entrada, salida y circulación de espectadores. El respaldo del Avatar alcanza los 48 centímetros de altura, frente a los aproximadamente 35 centímetros de los asientos actuales. Su geometría y la flexibilidad de los materiales buscan ofrecer mayor comodidad durante los partidos. A ello se suma otro cambio en la configuración de las gradas. La distancia media entre ejes de los asientos pasará de 45 a 50 centímetros, cinco centímetros adicionales que aumentarán la separación entre espectadores. No se trata únicamente de una modificación del asiento, sino de una decisión sobre la distribución del espacio disponible en el estadio. “Aspectos como la geometría del asiento, el espacio disponible o su integración en la grada tienen una incidencia directa en cómo el espectador vive varias horas dentro del estadio”, explica Pérez-Esparza. Detrás de estas mejoras hay también exigencias de resistencia y mantenimiento. El Avatar está fabricado con polipropileno copolímero en el asiento y el respaldo, mientras que las piezas sometidas a mayores esfuerzos incorporan poliamida reforzada con fibra de vidrio. Su resistencia ha sido certificada para uso público severo conforme a la norma UNE-EN 12727, mediante ensayos realizados por Aidimme. El diseño contempla, además, protección frente a la radiación ultravioleta y geometrías que evitan la acumulación de agua y suciedad, con el objetivo de prolongar la vida útil del equipamiento y facilitar su conservación. Soluciones adaptadas a las gradas Daplast también ha desarrollado un sistema de instalación mediante raíles metálicos que permite ajustar la separación entre asientos y reconfigurar determinadas zonas del estadio si fuera necesario. A diferencia de la fijación individual de cada localidad, esta solución reduce el número de perforaciones en el hormigón, simplifica las tareas de montaje y limita las intervenciones sobre el graderío. La compañía también ha diseñado anclajes específicos para adaptar los distintos modelos de asiento a las características de las estructuras de hormigón. En el nivel superior del estadio, el fabricante ha adaptado el Avatar para integrar el asiento con la baranda de protección frontal de cada fila. Esta configuración permite instalar ambos elementos conjuntamente y reducir los tiempos de montaje. Para el Valencia CF, el trabajo conjunto ha permitido abordar el equipamiento de las gradas más allá de la elección del asiento. “Hemos trabajado junto a Daplast en la definición de los diferentes modelos de butacas y su distribución en el estadio, buscando soluciones que se adapten a las características y necesidades de cada zona”, explica Solís. “El objetivo final es que el aficionado no tenga que pensar en el asiento, sino simplemente sentirse cómodo y disfrutar del espectáculo”, resume Pérez-Esparza.

articles.title: Champion weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin loses arm after motorbike crash
articles.summary: Commonwealth Games gold medallist Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has his right arm amputated above the elbow after a motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia.
articles.body:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin has had his right arm amputated above the elbow after a motorcycle accident in his native Malaysia.

The 21-year-old weightlifter was injured in a crash on Monday, according to local media reports.

Ayub Rahmat, president of the Malaysia Weightlifting Federation, said that Hafizuddin was conscious and in a stable condition in hospital in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.

"He is awake and smiling," Rahmat told AFP. "Physically his condition is improving but this incident has had a great impact on his future."

Hafizuddin won Commonwealth gold in the 88kg event in Glasgow in July and was hoping to compete at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

The Malaysian government has said it will cover all Hafizuddin's treatment and medical costs.

Ayub called it "a shock and a huge loss" and added: "We are already looking at how he can be integrated into the sport, including a future coaching role in weightlifting."

images.caption: Image caption, Hafizuddin broke the Commonwealth Games record in both the snatch and total categories in Glasgow

articles.title: Muere Sebastian Ebert, un skater de 16 años, tras una caída en Nashville
articles.standfirst: El adolescente sufrió un golpe en la cabeza al caer mientras practicaba hill bombing, una modalidad que consiste en bajar pendientes pronunciadas a gran velocidad
articles.summary: El adolescente sufrió un golpe en la cabeza al caer mientras practicaba hill bombing, una modalidad que consiste en bajar pendientes pronunciadas a gran velocidad
articles.body: Sebastian Ebert, de 16 años, falleció tras sufrir una caída con su monopatín en Two Rivers Greenway, un camino asfaltado de Nashville (Tennessee). Según la investigación preliminar del Departamento de Policía Metropolitana de Nashville, el joven bajaba a gran velocidad y sin casco por un tramo de fuerte pendiente que conduce hacia una planta de tratamiento de agua. Ebert se golpeó la cabeza al caer y fue trasladado al Skyline Medical Center, donde murió a causa de las lesiones. La policía investiga el fallecimiento como accidental. Ebert practicaba hill bombing, una modalidad arraigada en la cultura del skate que se suele practicar en calles y caminos asfaltados. La inclinación del terreno y la velocidad que alcanza la tabla durante el descenso dificultan el control y agravan las consecuencias de una caída. La muerte del adolescente ha causado conmoción en la comunidad del skate estadounidense y ha provocado numerosas muestras de cariño entre familiares y amigos. Ebert estudiaba en el Wilson Central High School, donde formaba parte del programa de formación culinaria. También tocaba la batería en varios grupos musicales de su comunidad religiosa. «Era un chico tranquilo, dulce y apacible al que todo el mundo quería», contó el pastor Barry Smith a la cadena local WKRN. Jennifer Ankney, directora del instituto, lo recordó así en The Tennessean. "Tenía una sonrisa cálida y era capaz de iluminar una habitación simplemente con su presencia". El instituto acogió un homenaje en su memoria. Sus abuelos pidieron a quienes quisieran tener un gesto con la familia que sustituyeran las flores por una donación a un fondo de becas para campamentos juveniles.

images.caption: Sebastian Ebert

articles.title: "She’s an amazing mum”: Anthony Joshua gets emotional as he opens up about ex girlfriend Nicole Osbourne after welcoming their second child
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua, the popular British boxer and 2012 Olympic super heavyweight gold medalist, seems to have stepped into the most exciting chapters of his
articles.body: Anthony Joshua, the popular British boxer and 2012 Olympic super heavyweight gold medalist, seems to have stepped into the most exciting chapters of his life as he has recently welcomed a baby girl into the world with his ex girlfriend, Nicole Osbourne. While both he and his ex girlfriend, Nicole Osbourne, have always tried to keep their relationship private, his recent comments on her have made many emotional.Anthony Joshua opens up about his ex girlfriend Nicole Osbourne as they welcome their second child togetherIn a recent interview with The Sun, the two time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua reflected on his ex girlfriend and also the mother of his two children, Nicole Osbourne, as he said, “She’s an amazing mum, and she’s already deeply in love.”The popular British boxer also opened up about his daughter’s birth as he said, “I feel it’s important for us men to support women…Now I’ve got a daughter, maybe me and her can set something up where we’re doing things with women, and just showing that feminine side of me. I want to bring women together, honour women, catering for them, you know.”Anthony Joshua added, “I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know? I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!”As per reports, Anthony Joshua and his ex girlfriend Nicole Osbourne were childhood sweethearts after having met in 2005 in their high school in Watford, United Kingdom, in 2005.The two have had an on off relationship since then and even welcomed their son together, Joseph ("JJ"), in 2015.While Nicole Osbourne and Anthony Joshua have again become parents, reports indicate that they are no longer romantically involved together, even after having two children.Though it is not known why exactly the two of them ended their relationship, there are speculations that have linked it to Anothony Joshua’s career commitments and busy professional life.Anthony Joshua reflects on the brutal car crash which killed his trainer and coachWhile Anthony Joshua has kept his focus on his career, he went through a pretty challenging time as he survived a fatal car crash on the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State, Nigeria, that killed his personal trainer Latif Ayodele and strength and conditioning coach Sina Ghami in December 2026.Authorities and court hearings pointed to excessive speed, a reported burst tyre, and an attempted overtaking maneuver that caused the SUV to lose control.In his interview with The Sun, Anthony Joshua also opened up about how his daughter’s birth was linked to the crash as he said, It was my duty – I wanted to bring life back into the world.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Panic Meter for Struggling NHL Teams During the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: We're almost two months into the NHL season, and we're quickly approaching American Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
We're almost two months into the NHL season, and we're quickly approaching American Thanksgiving.

As hockey fans know, American Thanksgiving is the best measuring stick we have when it comes to which teams will make the playoffs. As we await the day, we can't help but notice some absences from teams that many thought would either be in playoff spots or at least better off than they currently are.

As we take a look around the league, some of these teams are legitimately screwed, but some of these teams will persevere and get over their current struggles. Which of the struggling teams have a chance, and which need to hit the panic button?

For those who are wondering, we have a special ranking system specifically for each team.

Now that you're aware, let's get into it.

The Blackhawks got back on track with a 6-3 win against the also panicking Maple Leafs Tuesday, but as is the story of Chicago's season, it didn't come without a devastating blow.

We don't know the severity yet, but Connor Bedard is currently being evaluated for a right shoulder injury sustained in the game. He had his left shoulder surgically repaired in the past, and he missed 12 games last season with a right shoulder injury that didn't require surgery.

In layman's terms, this isn't good for the worst team in the Central.

This is Bedard's fourth season in the league. While there still wasn't immense pressure for the Blackhawks to make the playoffs headed into this season, there were some encouraging bouts of full-team play last season that made us feel like the team was at least going in the right direction.

We thought perhaps GM Kyle Davidson would've spent the offseason shopping for a high-end winger in his prime to complement Bedard, or at least some more viable center depth.

Instead, Davidson used the No. 4 overall pick in the 2026 draft as the centerpiece of a trade for Bowen Byram rather than addressing those needs up front. Byram is a solid, young defenseman with an intriguing ceiling, but Chicago paid a heavy price : that pick, a second-rounder and defenseman Louis Crevier, with forward Jordan Greenway also coming back in the deal.

Unfortunately, Byram got injured at the beginning of the season and has missed more than a month. On the bright side, his return could at least give the team a much-needed boost.

But it's clear the entire offense needs an overhaul and an upgrade. You expect the defense to be rockier on a more youthful team, but it's worth mentioning that the defense, too, has been brutal.

When it comes to Chicago, the panic isn't a concern about timing. It's the fact that they haven't quite used their rebuilding time to slowly but surely collect enough of the necessary pieces.

Artyom Levshunov is showing some promise in a rare bright spot of this season, but the Blackhawks have now invested three top-10 picks in their search for a No. 1 defenseman—two through the draft and one in the trade for Byram.

At this point, you're starting to wonder if and when things are going to click, and if and when Davidson is capable of giving the young core an adequate supporting cast.

Panic meter: 7.5 box-office flops (sorry, Showtime)

These Blue Jackets could only flail around the mushy middle until they arrived where they currently are: The non-mushy last-place spot at the bottom of the Metropolitan Division.

Their current five-game losing streak and latest 5-1 loss to the Islanders have displayed the utter lack of offensive power that has been the problem for the Blue Jackets for years.

The alarm bells started ringing when Zach Werenski and Kirill Marchenko both hinted last season that they weren't sure if they were going to stick with the franchise long-term. Werenski's still in Columbus and vetoed a trade to the Stars; meanwhile, the team's best goalscorer, Marchenko, was shipped to the Leafs.

Columbus is dead last in the NHL, averaging just 2.32 goals per game. It's the same old story for this franchise, but this time around it's like they're just rolling over and accepting their fate.

Panic meter: 8.5 "we like our group" interviews from GM Don Waddell

At this point, the Red Wings are less in "panic mode" and more sinking into "existential dread" territory. It's been 10 consecutive seasons without a playoff appearance, with the last seven of those featuring franchise legend Steve Yzerman failing to deliver on his "Yzerplan" as GM.

You thought that, at least once Red Wings ownership cut ties with Yzerman, the franchise would be able to go in a fresh direction with the rebuild and start rounding out the solid core he drafted. Instead, it took Dylan Larkin requesting a trade to force Yzerman out of the role way too late into the offseason, so the team was essentially in a holding pattern when it needed to make moves to improve the roster.

Now, Larkin still hasn't been traded; there's no new long-term GM, and the entire city of Detroit is essentially sitting on its hands while nothing gets done. It's infuriating.

Perhaps no NHL team was hyped up in the preseason more than the Sharks, and perhaps that was premature for a team still clearly needing many pieces.

Still, at 10-12-2, they're just one point out of a playoff spot in the Pacific Division. The proximity to the playoffs just doesn't feel too convincing right now if you're watching this team on a nightly basis, though.

The team-wide defense and chaotic semblance of a "system" are going to require much more work before this team becomes a true playoff threat. The aging and expensive blueline contracts they signed in the offseason continue to baffle as they search for the players who will stabilize their blue line and provide some traction in the neutral zone.

Beyond defense specifically, players look completely lost when Macklin Celebrini isn't on the ice. The Sharks need an identity beyond Celebrini, as great as he is. This will only happen once the blue line is stabilized and some of the younger core players feel comfortable taking some offensive chances and risks.

Oh, Toronto. Our precious, precious center of the hockey world has once again found itself in the middle of a mess.

The Leafs have dropped seven games in a row at this point, including their most recent 6-3 loss to the lowly Blackhawks.

What happened to the good vibes generated from the start of No. 1 overall draft pick Gavin McKenna's career and an awesome start to the season for Auston Matthews?

For one, the team is adjusting to major offseason overhauls and is coming off a non-playoff season. There shouldn't have been much panic about making the playoffs in the first place, but alas, this is the Leafs.

Sergei Bobrovsky has struggled to adjust to his new team. He owns rough stats all around, like a 3.65 goals-against average, an .874 save percentage, and 5.26 more goals allowed than expected.

This franchise shouldn't be panicking; it should be noting which big changes worked and which didn't. It should be back to the drawing board. But Auston Matthews and his contract aren't getting any younger, and there's obviously immense pressure to win a Cup with Matthews in the fold. Still, the pressure is unrealistic when the team is not even looking playoff-ready.

Wee-ooo, wee-ooo, wee-ooo. Do you hear that? That's the alarm sounding for the Mammoth, who once led the Central Division but are now mired in a six-game losing streak.

The streak has them now tied with the Jets for fifth in the division and out of a playoff spot. Meanwhile, they've won just three of their last 10. What the heck is happening?

Injuries all over the lineup haven't helped. Dylan Guenther, who scored 40 goals last season, is expected to miss two to four weeks with an upper-body injury. Veteran defenseman Nate Schmidt is also sidelined.

Still, there's something else going on: The goaltending has been atrocious. Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa have been one of the worst goaltending combinations in the league. The Mammoth have a .873 team save percentage, ranking 30th in the NHL.

There's a reason GM Bill Armstrong lobbied hard to acquire Connor Hellebuyck. But the Mammoth clearly didn't win that sweepstakes. If they can move on and still manage to acquire a better goaltender, they'll probably bounce back.

articles.title: 5 Ways The Rock's Survivor Series Return Could Shake Up WWE
articles.summary: Finally.
articles.body:
As announced Wednesday on The Pat McAfee Show on ESPN, The Rock will make his long-awaited return to WWE at Survivor Series: WarGames at Daikin Park in Houston on November 28.

It will be Rock's first appearance on WWE TV since he served as the catalyst for John Cena's heel turn at Elimination Chamber 2025.

Considering the company is also celebrating 30 years since The Great One's debut at the event, the timing is perfect. His return, though, brings great expectations that he will shake up WWE.

The Road to Rock vs. Roman (and What About Oba?)

The Rock returned to WWE television ahead of WrestleMania 40 with the intention of challenging Roman Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship in one of the few genuine dream matches professional wrestling still has to offer.

Instead, the audience demanded Cody Rhodes finish his story and win the title, which he did. Rock partnered with Reigns to defeat Rhodes and Seth Rollins on Night 1 of WrestleMania. The Great One then factored heavily into the final moments of the high-stakes, main event on Night 2.

Since then, the desire to see Reigns vs. Rock has resurfaced. Now, it would appear as though WWE is as close to delivering that match as it has been in the two years since it last tried.

Unfortunately, doing so would hinder Oba Femi's emergence as the next big thing in professional wrestling. The Ruler defeated Brock Lesnar in two of their three battles, retiring The Beast Incarnate at SummerSlam.

Since then, the path has been obvious: Femi vs. Reigns headlines WrestleMania 43, with the former crowned as the new world heavyweight champion.

That clearly cannot happen if Rock is coming back to set up a match with Reigns. If so, does WWE Creative face backlash again for setting someone up, only to have The Most Electrifying Man in Sports Entertainment pull the rug out from under him?

Speaking of Cody Rhodes, it is entirely possible The Rock stays away from Reigns and focuses his attention on The American Nightmare.

The last time we saw Rock, he was attempting to convince Rhodes to sell him his soul.

The babyface refused, and John Cena did instead.

Recently, though, Rhodes has embraced an edgier, darker side, even admitting just 48 hours after punting Randy Orton in the head that he "loved it." He has shown less patience and told SmackDown general manager Nick Aldis that he wants back in the Undisputed WWE Championship picture.

Could he get there by finally selling his soul to The Final Boss?

A Rhodes heel turn, like it or not, is the quickest path toward freshening up a character that some would say needs it. It would also give new layers to a character who fought so hard to achieve his lifelong dream but now, amid mounting pressure and frustration, realizes that he must take a shortcut to get back to the title that has become his obsession.

An angle where he embraces The Rock's help and, perhaps, betrays CM Punk to set up a WrestleMania 43 main event between them would be a headline-grabbing one and give the SmackDown main event scene some much-needed juice.

The Rock is destined to be greeted with a thunderous ovation at Survivor Series, not only because he is a generational star but also because fans have not seen him in well over a year.

What better way to really turn up the heat on The 946 ahead of WarGames against The Bloodline later in the show than by having Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Lucien Price, Bronco Nima and Jaida Parker attack him?

Not only does it get the red-hot heel faction on the same screen as a star of that magnitude, but it also heightens the personal issues between them and The Bloodline, considering Rock's place in the Samoan wrestling dynasty hierarchy.

It would be one last great angle to remind the audience that the group is dangerous and, to prove their catchphrase correct, "ain't nobody safe."

The number 30 is a nice round one. It is the perfect number for any major athlete to go out on, including a professional wrestler.

The Rock debuted three decades ago at Survivor Series, stunning the fans in Madison Square Garden by becoming the sole survivor for his team and eliminating Crush and Goldust consecutively to earn his first victory.

Since then, he weathered the storm of "die, Rocky, die" chants, became the most electrifying Superstar in the sport, moved on to Hollywood, came back, set pay-per-view buy-rate records with John Cena, and was integral in Cody Rhodes finishing his story. He has won championships, battled every major star on every grand stage and helped take wrestling to heights few could have ever imagined.

Simply put, The Rock has done it all in professional wrestling.

While it certainly is not something the WWE Universe wants to hear, The Great One could shake up the company by officially announcing his retirement from in-ring competition at the event where he debuted three decades earlier.

The Rock has already shaken up WWE merely by announcing his presence at Survivor Series. It is a rare occasion, so there is already a ton of speculation and interest in what he will do or say on November 28.

What if, and hear me out, he doesn't shake it up at all?

What if he goes to Houston, his music plays, the crowd erupts, he hits a "Finally," spouts catchphrases galore, calls WWE "home," thanks the WWE Universe for making him the People's Champion for the last 30 years, promises exciting things to come in the future and leaves?

He just peaces out, with no indication of any plans to come back or any angles setting up any future involvement.

See his Raw on Netflix debut for reference.

It is as possible and likely as any of the other four options, and that is what makes The Rock such a must-see Superstar because one never knows what to expect when he comes back to WWE television.

Some interaction with The Bloodline or The 946 feels like a given, though, so either a tease for Rock vs. Reigns or a beatdown from the heel faction feels like 1A and 1B as far as the most likely options to occur.

articles.title: El waterpolo no entiende de límites: "Tenía una depresión muy grande y esto me ha cambiado la vida"
articles.standfirst: Waterpolo Sin Límites es un proyecto para personas con discapacidad, mixto y social
articles.summary: Waterpolo Sin Límites es un proyecto para personas con discapacidad, mixto y social
articles.body: Un domingo cualquiera, a la una de la tarde, la piscina se llena de gorros, porterías y conversaciones que empiezan en el vestuario y acaban en el agua. Hay quien juega desde hace cuarenta años y quien nunca ha tocado un balón de waterpolo. Hay nadadores paralímpicos, exinternacionales y personas que hace apenas unos meses no sabían si volverían a nadar. Todos comparten algo. Todos comparten las ganas de formar un equipo. Así es Waterpolo Sin Límites, un proyecto nacido en Madrid que quiere sacar del anonimato el waterpolo para personas con discapacidad. MARCA estuvo en su jornada de puertas abiertas y se sentó en el vestuario con algunos de sus protagonistas. La historia empieza en Madrid en los años 80. Un grupo de nadadores con discapacidad, entre ellos Alberto y Roberto, decidió tirarse a la piscina con un balón. "Hubo gente que, de forma altruista, se apuntó", recuerda Félix Fernández, waterpolista olímpico en Los Ángeles 84 y hoy entrenador del proyecto. Aquel grupo jugó durante años, pero la actividad acabó apagándose. El impulso para recuperarla llegó desde Cataluña. Allí, la Federación Catalana de Deportes de Personas con Discapacidad Física (FCEDF) puso en marcha en 2023 la primera Liga Catalana de waterpolo para personas con discapacidad, con el CN Barcelona, el CN Sabadell y el CN Terrassa. Entre sus organizadores estaba Gabi Villarubia, "Villapela", exwaterpolista internacional con una discapacidad severa. "En Cataluña se lanzaron una serie de equipos hace poco y, gracias a eso, lo conseguimos relanzar aquí también", explica Félix. Toñi se puso en contacto con el impulsor del proyecto en Cataluña, Gabi Villarubia, y con Félix en el 2025 formamos el Team para impulsar el waterpolo para personas con discapacidad. Félix, Luis y Toñi lideran el proyecto. Con el apoyo de la IMANcorp Foundation, que se sumó en octubre de 2025, el grupo trabaja con clubes y federaciones para crear la primera liga nacional de waterpolo paralímpico. La idea es empezar con equipos de Madrid e ir sumando otras comunidades. Toñi es trabajadora social y en el proyecto se le juntan dos pasiones. "El waterpolo, aunque no soy jugadora, y mi profesión", cuenta. Reconoce que las redes sociales han dado al proyecto un empujón que nadie esperaba, y reparte el mérito: "Sin los impulsores, esto no habría salido". El equipo ya sabe lo que es competir. Participó en el Torneo Internacional de Terrassa y terminó en quinta posición. "Es un deporte minoritario, pero fantástico", resume Toñi. El objetivo a largo plazo es ambicioso: llegar algún día a los Juegos Paralímpicos, de los que el waterpolo todavía no forma parte. El contexto invita a soñar. En octubre de 2026, la selección española de waterpolo de personas con discapacidad física disputó en Potenza (Italia) el primer Torneo Internacional de Waterpolo Paralímpico, junto a Italia y Hungría. La charla empieza con risas, como no puede ser de otra forma. Emilio, Roberto, Luis y Alberto formaron parte de aquel primer grupo de los años 80. "Éramos nadadores y nos surgió la idea. Ahora, con mucha ilusión, retomamos esto", cuenta Emilio. Roberto lo recuerda con humor: "Jugábamos y nos tomábamos unas cañas cuando perdíamos". Ahora vuelve al agua con una sonrisa: "Estoy encantado de estar aquí con mis viejos amigos". La historia de Alberto es distinta. Empezó a jugar sin ninguna discapacidad, pero una operación le cambió la vida. "Ahora ya soy paralímpico", dice. Joaquín juega en equipo amateur convencional, y ahora juega en los dos equipos a la vez. Siempre ha echado de menos referentes para jugar a waterpolo paralímpico. Fran es uno de los rostros más recientes. Hace cinco meses sufrió un accidente y ahora vive en Toledo. Antes de eso, el waterpolo lo era todo: "He sido cuatro veces máximo goleador de España. El waterpolo es mi vida". Lejos de rendirse, se ha propuesto probarlo todo: "Ahora estoy practicando todos los deportes que puedo". Luis, jugador y nadador paralímpico, tiene un objetivo muy concreto: "A ver si conseguimos un grupo de gente para poder tener un equipo". Y da la cita a quien quiera sumarse: "Entrenamos los domingos de una a tres". El testimonio más emocionante llega de Juan. Hace dos años sufrió un accidente de trabajo. Hasta entonces, el agua le era ajena: "Nunca había visto el agua". Empezó a nadar y hoy dice hacer 60 kilómetros en coche para ello. "Estoy encantado. Me ha cambiado la vida. Tenía una depresión muy grande y conoceros ha sido una superación", cuenta, mirando a sus compañeros. "Estoy deseando que llegue el domingo para venir". También hay quien llega por curiosidad. Sara es nadadora y nunca ha probado el waterpolo. Esteban, nadador de Pozuelo, al igual que Sara, viene con un grupo de su zona. Para ellos está pensada esta jornada. Félix no esconde las dificultades. "Es complicado, porque si el waterpolo ya es minoritario, el paralímpico lo es más aún", admite. Hoy solo existe una liga, la catalana, y el proyecto madrileño quiere romper ese techo. "La idea es ir uniendo gente y tener un grupo asiduo con objetivos comunes, para participar en torneos y poder crear una liga nacional, que de momento no existe. Queremos hacer una liga competitiva", explica. En esta jornada, se echó de menos a jugadores que estaban jugando en sus respectivos equipos: Rodri (13 años) jugador del Rivas, Jorge Nérida del Madridejos, Enrique Navas, es triatleta, pero ya está buscando posición en el arco, y Teresa Pérez que está lesionada. El camino acaba de empezar. "Estamos en pañales, en contacto con las federaciones", reconoce. Por eso la prioridad ahora es sumar jugadores. "Estamos en periodo de captación", dice el entrenador, que lanza una invitación a quien lea estas líneas: "La idea es que lo probéis, que veáis cómo os sentís, si os ilusiona o no". En el vestuario, la respuesta parece clara. Los veteranos han vuelto, los nuevos quieren repetir y Juan ya cuenta los días para el domingo. El waterpolo para personas con discapacidad sigue siendo un deporte casi invisible, pero en Madrid ya hay un grupo dispuesto a demostrar que, en el agua, los límites los pone cada uno. El no puedo no existe. Waterpolo Sin Límites entrena los domingos de 13:00 a 15:00 en Centro deportivo Municipal Margot Moles. Las personas interesadas pueden contactar con el proyecto a través de @wpsinlimites (Instagram) o correo electrónico: wpsinlimites@gmail.com

articles.title: College Basketball Catchup: Top-25 Upsets, A Triple-Double, Notre Dame's Star
articles.summary: Multiple ranked-ranked upsets, a triple-double, 11 3s from one shooter, Hannah Hidalgo is on fire and more from Wednesday's college basketball action.
articles.body: A pair of top-3 men's teams were upset on Wednesday. A TCU guard pulled off a triple-double. Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo has been relentless to begin her senior year. Here's what you need to know from Wednesday's slate of college basketball: 1 Name To Know: Ivan Kharchenkov Ivan Kharchenkov is in his second collegiate season, but he’s played high-level basketball for longer than that, having also spent time in the EuroLeague with Bayern for two years. The 6-foot-7 forward has had an excellent start to his sophomore campaign with No. 12-ranked Arizona, and was the Wildcats' leading scorer against No. 3 UConn on Wednesday in an 85-79 upset win. Arizona barely touched its bench, giving all but 19 minutes to its starters, and Kharchenkov led with 39 minutes and 20 points on 7-for-12 shooting while pulling down five rebounds, dishing out seven assists and picking up a pair of steals. Kharchenkov had a solid freshman season with 10.4 points per game, but didn’t excel in any one stat. The start of the 2026-2027 season has been a different story: He’s averaging 22.6 points, 8.0 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.8 steals through five games, and has jumped his shot attempts per game from 7.8 per to 14.4. Arizona needed to replace Brayden Burries’ production somehow now that he’s in the NBA, and so far, so good, thanks to Kharchenkov. Upsets, Chaos, Confusion: Houston Takes Down Florida No. 8 Houston did its part in ensuring a new-look poll next week, as it took down No. 1 Florida, 86-76. This was the Cougars' first win over a No. 1-ranked team since 1978, when Houston defeated Arkansas, 84-75, and with it the three top-ranked teams in men’s basketball have all lost this week. (And four of the top five: 6-0 No. 4 Virginia won its matchup against Old Dominion, however.) Florida actually led at halftime, 40-37, but Houston erupted for 49 points in the second half, including 13 points from senior guard Dedan Thomas Jr., who scored a game-high 30 on 10-for-17 shooting and a perfect 8-for-8 showing from the free throw line. This was Houston’s first win against a ranked opponent this year, and the Cougars pulled it off despite junior guard Boogie Fland — who had exited Florida’s game on Tuesday after eight minutes thanks to aggravating his shoulder injury — playing for 29 minutes. Houston held Fland to just four points, and he fouled out with 3:10 left on the clock. Top Performance: Jadyn Wooten TCU’s Jadyn Wooten channeled ex-Horned Frogs star Olivia Miles on Wednesday. The junior guard and Oklahoma State transfer produced a triple-double against UT Arlington, with 18 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds across 33 minutes, helping the No. 15 Horned Frogs blow out the Mavericks, 96-48. That was the first triple-double of Wooten’s career, as well as her first-ever game with at least 10 rebounds, and the second-most assists she’s logged in a game. The one knock against her performance was that Wooten shot just 5-for-13 from the field, but she sank all eight free-throw attempts and did plenty elsewhere to make up for that. Men's Scoring Leader: Kam Burton Before this month, senior guard Kam Burton had never attempted more than 11 3-pointers in a game. For La Salle on Wednesday, the SFA transfer made 11 from deep, breaking the program record of nine and then adding two more to put it just a little further out of reach. Burton ended his night with 36 points to lead all Division I scorers and set a new career-high, as well. He had never scored more than 20 points in a game, but Burton blew well past that mark on Wednesday in an 88-61 win over Coppin State. Women's Scoring Leader: Janai Jordan Sophomore Janai Jordan is in her first season of Division I basketball, as West Florida played in Division II during her freshman campaign. The transition seems to be going well enough for both Jordan and the Argonauts, as she led all Division I women’s players with 34 points on Wednesday against Spring Hill in a 71-58 win. Now, to be fair, Spring Hill is Division II, but UWF is 3-3 and has been mixing in D-I competition, too, to prepare for Atlantic Sun conference play. The Argonauts will need more games like this one from Jordan to make any noise there. Before You Go: Hannah Hidalgo Is On FIRE USC’s JuJu Watkins might be the favorite to go first overall in the 2027 WNBA Draft, but Notre Dame’s Hannah Hidalgo could have something to say about that before this season is over. On Wednesday, the senior guard shot 7-for-13 and went to the free throw line 18 times en route to a game-high 31 points against Southern, which the Fighting Irish won 95-47. Hidalgo sank 16 shots from the charity stripe, giving her the ACC’s all-time career record for free throws in the process. She also had four rebounds, four assists and seven steals. Those 31 points raised her Division I-leading average to 28.8 points per game, and Hidalgo is also the ACC leader in steals with 5.2 per game. Less than a week ago, Hidalgo became the first-ever college basketball player — men’s or women’s — with 2,500 points, 500 rebounds, 500 assists and 500 steals in their career. There’s a lot of season left, but performances like this will make both the national Player of the Year Award and No. 1 draft pick discussions lively ones. articles.title: La espina que aún duele en el Barcelona por Luis Díaz: Deco lo señala como su gran fichaje frustrado
articles.standfirst: El fichaje que el Barcelona más lamenta: Deco señala a Luis Díaz
articles.summary: El fichaje que el Barcelona más lamenta: Deco señala a Luis Díaz
articles.body: El Barcelona sigue lamentando no haber podido concretar el fichaje de Luis Díaz, el delantero colombiano que terminó en el Bayern de Múnich. Más de un año después, el director deportivo culé, Deco, reconoció que Lucho fue la incorporación que más le dolió no cerrar durante su gestión. A mediados de 2025, Díaz apareció como uno de los principales objetivos del Barcelona para reforzar su ataque. El club catalán lo siguió durante varios mercados, pero fue en el verano de 2025 cuando la opción tomó mayor fuerza. En una entrevista con Catalunya Ràdio, Deco fue consultado por el fichaje que más le dolió no poder concretar y no dudó en responder: "Luis Díaz, sin duda". El dirigente lo eligió incluso por delante de Julián Álvarez y Bernardo Silva, dos nombres que también sonaron con fuerza en ese periodo de pases. La operación no prosperó por una combinación de factores: las exigencias económicas del Liverpool y las limitaciones financieras del Barcelona impidieron llegar a un acuerdo. Finalmente, Díaz terminó fichando por el Bayern de Múnich, mientras el Barça optó por incorporar a Marcus Rashford a préstamo. La frustración del Barça tiene sentido: Díaz era visto como un refuerzo ideal para un ataque que necesitaba mayor profundidad, desequilibrio y capacidad de desbordamiento. Su perfil, con velocidad, regate y gol, encajaba con las necesidades del equipo catalán. Sin embargo, la realidad económica del club y la postura del Liverpool hicieron que la negociación no avanzara. Así, el colombiano terminó en la Bundesliga, donde ha continuado demostrando su nivel en un equipo de alto rendimiento. Díaz, cerca del regreso En la actualidad, Luis Díaz atraviesa la recta final de su recuperación tras la lesión sufrida el 21 de octubre, durante el empate del Bayern ante el Arsenal por Champions League. El técnico Vincent Kompany descartó su participación en el duelo ante Colonia, pero anticipó que podría volver a disputar minutos en los próximos siete días. “Lucho está muy bien. Ha completado una buena semana de trabajo. Aún es demasiado pronto para que pueda jugar mañana. Durante los próximos siete días estaremos en condiciones de que vuelva a disputar minutos”, explicó Kompany. Un fichaje que quedó pendiente Para el Barcelona, la historia de Luis Díaz quedó como una de las grandes oportunidades perdidas de los últimos mercados. Para el colombiano, en cambio, el Bayern representó una nueva etapa de consolidación en la élite europea, mientras el club catalán sigue mirando hacia atrás y preguntándose qué habría pasado si la operación se hubiera cerrado.
