articles.title: The World Darts Championship is now the 'incentive' for Luke Littler after Grand Slam of Darts loss, says Wayne Mardle
articles.summary: Sky Sports Darts' Wayne Mardle believes Luke Littler has to use winning the World Darts Championship as his motivation following his Grand Slam of Darts loss; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
articles.body:
Littler was attempting to become the third player ever to win the Wolverhampton event three times in a row alongside Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen.

However, he came up against an incredible performance from Wattimena, in which he was hitting T20s for fun and averaged over 101.

With Littler also missing the Players Championship, which is the last major before Alexandra Palace in December, the next time we will see Littler on the TV stage is when he plays his opening Worlds match on Friday December 11 as the reigning champion, live on Sky Sports .

Littler went into 2026 targeting a clean sweep of majors and while he won the Premier League, Masters, UK Open, and World Matchplay, his loss in the second round at the World Series Finals to Dirk van Duijvenbode has started a run without a major win.

He has since not defended his World Grand Prix title, Grand Slam title, or clinched the European Championship, which has eluded him.

For Mardle, Littler has to put everything else to one side, use his time away to get fresh, practice, and win the major that just has something a bit different to the rest.

"There is no doubt that every player gets more motivated. The Worlds is different," Mardle said.

"The run-up is different and the build-up to it is gigantic.

"He went basically nine months into the year holding this belief and everyone else thinking he's going to do the clean sweep.

"So it was nine months of all this and then it ends, but the Worlds is out on its own. The incentive is that it is the Worlds. That is all the incentive you need. It is the biggest and it is the best event.

"If he loses in that then he will have gone four months without a major.

"The Worlds is the one, and Michael van Gerwen said this for years: what is the point in winning anything else? You only need to win this one.

"I think that is just the same with Luke's mentality."

'You are better winning the Players Championship'

The talk has already turned to whether Littler's time away from the TV spotlight will be a positive or a negative as he attempts to become the second player ever, alongside Taylor, to have won the World Darts Championship three or more times in a row.

Mardle insists that, while it would be better for Littler to be heading into the Worlds as a potential Players Championship winner after his loss at the Grand Slam, if he brings his A-game, it is his to lose.

"I don't know how he really feels about losing here at the Grand Slam but what I do think going forward, because he's not playing in the Players Championship, so his next outing will be at the Worlds.

"This is the way that I would frame it - would he be better not playing, or would he be better winning the Players Championship? You are better winning the Players Championship.

"But that is the kind of situation that you don't know. You don't know if he goes to the Players Championship, wins it or loses.

"If he loses, it is like maybe he shouldn't have gone to that, in hindsight and everything else.

"I really believe for Luke, if he can turn up fresh, if he can turn up ready, if he can turn up with anywhere near his A-game, he probably wins the Worlds again. That will be three times on the bounce by the age of 20, which is ridiculous."

'It reminds me of trying to beat Taylor'

Wattimena picked up the biggest win of his career against Littler at the Grand Slam but it is not the first time he has come out on top against 'The Nuke' as he beat him in August on the way to winning a Players Championship title.

Wattimena said that win gave him confidence and reinforced that Littler is "not a robot" and Mardle believes that win can be credited for the performance we saw from the Dutchman in the Grand Slam.

"I know this is a thing. I was about when Phil Taylor was hardly ever beaten and until you actually beat him, you don't believe you can," he said.

"You see others beat him, there were loads throughout the years. There was Andy Callaby. Adrian Gray beat him. There were others that beat him that were not as good as me.

"I remember thinking why can't I ever beat Phil? It is not until you do that you know that someone's not a robot.

"So that win was massive for Jermaine and it was one of the reasons why he won yesterday.

"Now going forward after yesterday, he can beat anyone on that stage. Luke Humphries has to watch out if he plays Jermaine. Gerwyn Price, they should all watch out now.

"It is really important to have belief. Now he has got it and he has got the ability."

Watch the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live on Sky Sports. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Dodgers Sign Former Top Pitching Prospect to Minor League Deal
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers signed righth-handed pitcher Tink Hence to a minor league deal, per MiLB Central's Chase Ford. The post Dodgers Sign Former Top Pitch...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers signed righth-handed pitcher Tink Hence to a minor league deal, per MiLB Central's Chase Ford.

The St. Louis Carindals drafted Hence, now 24, in the second competitive balance round of the 2020 draft with the No. 63 pick, and he was the No. 2 prospect in the system at one point.

St. Louis designated him for assignment in August before outrighting him to the Florida Complex League, and the right-hander elected free agency after the end of the season.

Hence pitched just eight times in rookie ball during the 2021 season, but put together a solid season the following year. He pitched 16 times in Class-A, allowing just eight earned runs in 52.1 innings pitched while striking out 81 batters.

He made his debut in High-A the following year, making 11 appearances as a starter with the Peoria Chiefs while posting a 2.81 ERA. The right-hander moved up to Double-A that same season, but struggled to post similar results with a 5.47 ERA through 12 appearances.

Hence settled in the following year, making 20 Double-A starts while slicing his ERA in half from the year prior, ending the season with a 2.71 mark. Several injuries impacted his availability, though, dealing with shoulder, chest and lat tightness.

The following year he suffered a rib cage strain which kept him out until May, and shoulder and pectoral injuries in the latter half of 2025 limited him to just eight starts. He returned in a bullpen role in 2026, and looked a shadow of himself in Triple-A. He had a 6.64 ERA and struck out 20 batters in 20.1 innings pitched.

Through 94 career appearances, Hence has a 3.50 ERA through 277.2 innings pitched, striking out 347 batters.

He still had a solid whiff rate in 2026, though his control suffered and his strikeout rate and fastball velocity dropped far lower than expected.

Will Tink Hence Play For the Dodgers Next Year?

Hence likely won't appear for the Dodgers in 2027, though his involvement isn't impossible.

The Dodgers struggled with injuries to their pitching depth in 2024, 2025 and 2026, so if they find themselves in a pinch, Hence may be able to step in and do a job.

The right-hander's main focus with the Dodgers will be returning to his for before suffering his various injuries, and will hope a healthy season is enough to put him on the team's radar next year.

articles.title: Michigan football wide receiver Andrew Marsh charged with indecent exposure
articles.summary: Michigan wide receiver Andrew Marsh has been charged with indecent exposure over a February incident in which he allegedly flashed a female delivery driver
articles.body:
Michigan football wide receiver Andrew Marsh has been charged with indecent exposure for an off-campus incident in early February.

According to a release from Pittsfield Township Police & Fire Department on Thursday, Nov. 19, the Washtenaw County (Michigan) Prosecutor's office authorized a misdemeanor complaint of indecent exposure on Oct. 14.

A notice to appear was generated on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and Marsh is scheduled for a pre-trial hearing on Dec. 4.

"We were just made aware of an incident involving Andrew Marsh," Michigan football spokesman Dave Ablauf said in a statement to The Detroit News , a part of the USA TODAY Network. "We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available, but we are unable to comment further due to the on-going case."

According to the Pittsfield Township Police & Fire Department release, the department was contacted on Feb. 2 by a female food service delivery driver who claimed that during a delivery, the door was answered by a man who had a blanket draped over his shoulders and was unclothed beneath it. As the complainant turned to leave, the man pulled the blanket apart, exposing his genitals.

After she left the residence, the complainant said she received a message from the customer in which he said that she was attractive and asked if she would return to the address.

According to online court records, the incident occurred on Feb. 1. Pittsfield police officers contacted the male, who confirmed he received the delivery and subsequently was identified as the suspect. The male is listed as 18 years old at the time of the incident. Marsh turned 19 on Feb. 2.

As a freshman last season, Marsh was Michigan's leading wide receiver, catching 45 passes for 651 yards and four touchdowns. This season, the Texas native has 48 receptions for 459 yards and a touchdown.

The charge against Marsh is the latest bit of bad news for a Michigan program that is enduring a disastrous first season under coach Kyle Whittingham. Heading into their Week 12 game against No. 4 UCLA, the Wolverines are 5-5 and have the eighth-worst scoring offense at the FBS level, averaging just 18.3 points per game. If Michigan is unable to beat UCLA or No. 17 Ohio State, it will finish a full season with a losing record for the first time since 2014.

articles.title: Patriots Must Draft Nick Marsh To Fix Maye’s Wide Receiver Room
articles.summary: With Drake Maye out for the season, the Patriots need a new weapon. ESPN's mock draft points to Nick Marsh as the answer for New England.
articles.body:
The Patriots are staring down a massive hole at wide receiver, and the solution might already be in the draft. With starting quarterback Drake Maye most likely sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, the team cannot afford to wait on its current roster to figure itself out. A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs have played just 10 combined games due to injuries, and neither has posted a 100-yard performance yet. This lack of production forces DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins into roles they were not built to fill. On Wednesday, an early 2027 mock draft by ESPN's Jordan Reid projected New England using the 16th overall pick to take Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh. This move addresses a critical need before the next offseason even begins.

The Patriots have failed to find a consistent target for their young quarterback, and Marsh offers a physical profile that changes the equation. Reid wrote that "Marsh is a stout, powerful receiver at 6-foot-3 and 210 pounds whose play strength is the hallmark of his game." This size allows him to line up in the slot or outside and overpower defensive backs, a skill set New England desperately lacks right now. The Indiana star has already demonstrated his value this season by gaining 307 of his 749 receiving yards after the catch. He also is an excellent run blocker, which fits the gritty identity the team is trying to build under Mike Vrabel. Drafting him would give the offense a true go-to weapon who can handle the physical toll of the NFL.

The urgency to add talent is not just about the draft; it is about the immediate reality of the season. Team captain Kevin Byard dropped a hint about the severity of the quarterback situation on Tuesday. "Our quarterback's out, and he's probably going to be out for the rest of the season," Byard told WEEI's Rich & Ken, according to Yahoo Sports . While the team has not officially confirmed the timeline, the reports point to a fractured ankle that requires extensive recovery. This injury forces the Patriots to look at the future with a clear eye. Even if Brown and Doubs return healthy next year, the roster needs depth.

The second half of the 2026 season will dictate how the front office views the wide receiver room. If Brown cannot display his star talent in the remaining games, the need for a younger star option becomes undeniable. In the mock, Reid observed that Marsh went as the fourth wide receiver, trailing Jeremiah Smith, Charlie Becker, and Jackson Harris. The Patriots sit at 5-5 entering their Week 11 bye and hold the 16th pick if the standings hold. Because the Brown trade obligates them to send the Eagles their 2028 first-rounder, this 2027 selection becomes even more critical. The team must get behind backup Tommy DeVito for now, but securing a top-tier receiver for Maye's return is the only path forward.

articles.title: Dortmund sweating over fitness of key trio ahead of Gladbach trip
articles.summary: Waldemar Anton, Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka all missed out on representing their respective countries during the international break due to muscul...
articles.body:
Waldemar Anton, Serhou Guirassy and Carney Chukwuemeka all missed out on representing their respective countries during the international break due to muscular problems.

And, as Borussia Dortmund coach Niko Kovač revealed during a press conference on Thursday, the trio remain doubtful for his side's away game against Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

"We'll see today or tomorrow whether they will be fit enough for the weekend," Kovač said.

The coach did not rule out any of the three featuring, but neither did he guarantee their availability.

"We're saying it's fifty-fifty at the moment."

With the exception of Samuele Inacio, who is carrying a minor knock after representing Italy U21s, all other players returned from international duty in "fairly good shape," Kovač added.

Saturday's game at Borussia-Park kicks off at 15:30 CEST.

articles.title: Rick Stockstill dreamed of coaching FSU. This homecoming, it's reality
articles.summary: Interim coach Rick Stockstill leads the Florida State Seminoles during homecoming, a full circle moment for the former FSU football player.
articles.body:
Florida State 's Homecoming game against North Carolina State carries plenty of storylines.

It's about the players, beating the Wolfpack , earning bowl eligibility with their third consecutive win and celebrating the university's heritage with students, alumni and supporters.

But it's also impossible to ignore what Saturday at Doak Campbell Stadium at 3:30 p.m. means for interim head coach Rick Stockstill, even if he doesn't want Homecoming to be about him.

His family and former FSU teammates understand that.

And this Homecoming gives them something new to remember: one of their own leading the Seminoles onto Bobby Bowden Field.

"I am filled with so many emotions," Bonnie Good, Stockstill's sister, told the Tallahassee Democrat. "I am sure I will cry happy tears watching Rick lead the team on the field. This has been a lifelong dream of his to coach at FSU, ever since he played for Bobby Bowden and became a coach himself. He is so deserving, and I give all the glory to God for giving him this opportunity."

Homecoming means plenty to Rick Stockstill, former teammates

Stockstill arrived at FSU from Fernandina Beach as part of Bobby Bowden's first recruiting class in 1977, a year after Bowden came to Tallahassee from West Virginia. The Seminoles had endured four consecutive losing seasons, but Stockstill and his classmates helped change that, becoming part of the foundation for FSU's rise to national prominence.

Nearly five decades later, that bond remains.

The group stayed in contact over the years and began holding annual reunions in 1993, gathering at Neptune Beach for the past 15 years. What once centered primarily on former teammates has grown into a multigenerational tradition, with wives, children and grandchildren joining the reunions.

This weekend, many of them will gather again in Tallahassee. They will swap stories and laugh about the old days, only this time they also will watch their former quarterback lead the Seminoles from the sideline.

"I've cherished every second of it," said Stockstill, who was named the Seminoles' interim head coach after FSU fired Mike Norvell on Nov. 1. "I just love the opportunity and how I can impact these players and staff and the program here in a short period of time."

Meet FSU interim coach Rick Stockstill, an FSU Athletics Hall of Famer

Stockstill has quickly put his stamp on the program with his passion, authenticity and humility. His best friend and former FSU teammate Brent Brock believes those qualities help explain why players and staff have responded to him.

"He's got a title, and that's all he has," said Brock, who also coached with Stockstill at Middle Tennessee State. "He's just one of them regular dudes in there. Everybody from the secretaries to the interns, the recruiting staff, equipment staff … he just wants to be one of them. That's kind of like he's always been and always will be."

About 15 members of Stockstill's immediate family also are expected to attend the game, including his wife, Sara; their son, Brent, an offensive quality control coach with the Indianapolis Colts, and his family; daughter Emily; and Sara's sister, Renae, among others.

Legendary FSU defensive coordinator Mickey Andrews understands the emotional pull of having the opportunity to coach at one's alma mater. He is thrilled that Stockstill and former FSU linebacker Ernie Sims, now the Seminoles' interim defensive coordinator, have experienced it.

Andrews played at Alabama under legendary coach Bear Bryant and twice had opportunities to return to his alma mater as a coach. He ultimately decided he already had the better job, coordinating Bowden's defense at FSU.

"I think, as a player and as a coach, you always want the opportunity to go back to your alma mater," Andrews said.

Rick Stockstill's family, teammates enjoying the moment

Stockstill's coaching future remains uncertain. He said Monday that he hopes the Seminoles' late-season turnaround leads to another head coaching opportunity, whether at FSU or elsewhere. Stockstill would also welcome the chance to remain at FSU under a new head coach, citing his love for his alma mater and the lasting influence Bowden had on him.

Brock believes Stockstill remains built for the job.

"The coaching profession, you're really younger than your age just because you stay young and stay motivated for what your mission is," Brock said. "And this game is not just to win ball games, but to develop young people. They keep you invigorated. They keep you young.

"And in all fairness, he's probably a late-40s, early-50s guy with his juice."

Following homecoming, the Seminoles close out their regular season against state rival Florida, Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:30 p.m. Doak Campbell Stadium. After missing the postseason in 2024 (2-10) and 2025 (5-7), they need one win in their final two games to become bowl eligible. FSU's 36-year bowl streak in 2018, followed by four missed postseasons in six years.

Whatever comes next, Stockstill's homecoming continues Saturday when, nearly five decades after arriving at FSU as a young quarterback in Bowden's first recruiting class, he leads the Seminoles onto Bobby Bowden Field at Doak Campbell Stadium for the first time as their head coach.

His family and former teammates will be there to see it.

For a group that has spent decades reuniting to remember where their journey at FSU began, this weekend gives them something new to embrace and enjoy.

"It's going to be a good deal," Brock said.

Where: Doak Campbell Stadium, Tallahassee, Florida

J im Henry is the award-winning sports editor of the Tallahassee Democrat. Email him at jjhenry@tallahassee.com.
